V1 includes Appendix A.1–A.6; v2 ends after the references despite mentioning supplementary material. The omissions identified below concern the supplied v2.pdf, without assuming what an unavailable supplement contains.

after.justification: V2 reports TR2M benchmark results and ablations in Tables 1–5. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical outcomes of the work.

before.justification: V1 reports original TR2M benchmark results, zero-shot evaluations, ablations and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendix.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes training-free transductive fusion and approximately ten-point improvements over CLIP. V2 broadens the contribution to adaptive, prior-free integration across model families, domains and inference settings, and explicitly claims applicability to black-box models accessed through APIs. Its novelty claim expands from VFM/VLM complementarity in transductive ZSL to foundation-model integration in zero-shot classification generally.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking adaptive weights to model agreement, interpreting modest gains among strong models and larger gains under model-quality disparities. It introduces modality-gap, model-subset and efficiency interpretations. V1's explicit limitation concerning fixed/equal weighting is replaced by claims of adaptive weighting, while future-work discussion shifts toward semantic ensemble learning and multi-view clustering.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the deferred code-release promise with a repository link and adds model-variant, weight-initialization and inductive-inference details in Appendix 7.2, directing readers to code for dataset templates. Most basic implementation information is retained: 224×224 center crops, fixed prompts, epsilon 0.01 and a 24GB RTX 4090. Repository availability is stated in the PDF but was not externally verified.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original 11 datasets, expands remote-sensing coverage from EuroSAT to ten datasets, and adds five medical-pathology datasets. It also evaluates inductive generalization to unseen instances alongside transduction. The claimed 26 benchmarks comprise overlapping domain groups: EuroSAT appears in both the natural-image and remote-sensing groups.

Domain-specific individual models and simple ensemble comparators are also added.

It adds DINOv3 and additional model combinations, clustering-accuracy evaluations, and time/memory measurements. Appendix Table 6 specifies adaptation before ensembling. Exact inductive split sizes are not supplied, limiting reproduction of the new protocol.

Visual-source and joint-learning ablations extend questions already tested in v1. V1's feature-concatenation comparison, explicit single-visual-source ablations, epsilon/lambda sensitivity sweeps and convergence-loss plot disappear. The Pets visualization is replaced by EuroSAT/Food101 visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, error bars or significance tests. V2's additional dataset averages and runtime measurements do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1 reports OTFusion averages of 74.95% and 70.45% for its two backbone settings. V2 Table 1 reports revised configurations, including 75.7% for CLIP-1+DINOv2 and 77.8% for CLIP-1+DINO(v2+v3), plus extensive new inductive and domain-specific results. These are not controlled same-setting improvements. Table 5 newly reports 71.8% fixed-weight versus 73.1% adaptive-weight accuracy.

M1.justification: V1 uses a linear OT objective with fixed model weights. V2 introduces squared agreement terms and MM-based adaptive weights, substantially changing optimization (Section 3.2.2 and Appendix 6). It also adds inductive inference using learned GMM parameters and fusion weights. Multi-model probability fusion and joint GMM/transport updates already existed in v1.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements and substantial portions of the method and experimental narrative are rewritten. This exceeds a method-name or terminology edit.

P2.justification: V2 adds a pipeline diagram, radial performance/clustering charts, grouped ablation bars and domain-specific comparison tables. The original backbone comparison and ablation tables are substantially reorganized, including separate transductive and inductive displays. Sensitivity and loss plots are removed, and the qualitative visualization becomes a two-dataset figure. Table styling and document layout also change extensively.

V2 adds domain-specific foundation models, newer adaptation methods and MM-related literature, and explicitly acknowledges inspiration from TransCLIP. V1's discussion of DINO-assisted prompt learning and its MoE positioning are removed.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's linear OT formulation and alternating updates, v2 derives a quadratic objective, a tangent minorizer in Theorem 1, adaptive coefficients and an MM optimization scheme. It adds a stationary-point convergence claim and computational-complexity analysis. The convergence argument does not establish that the stated GMM update increases the surrogate, so the added guarantee remains insufficiently justified.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's stated fixed-weight limitation and substantially strengthens the previously limited evidence for heterogeneous-model fusion through adaptive-weight controls, domain-specific ensembles, inductive evaluation and measured computational costs. These gains outweigh the loss of sensitivity analyses and reporting weaknesses. Nevertheless, the convergence justification is incomplete, Table 7 swaps the MUSK/PLIP baseline values relative to Table 3, and the claimed 6.9-point lead conflicts with Table 1: CLIP-1+DINOv3 exceeds GTA-CLIP by 2.9 points.

V1 has no appendix; v2 includes supplementary optimization, implementation and experimental material in Sections 6–8.

before.justification: V1 reports original OTFusion benchmark results, component ablations, parameter-sensitivity experiments and convergence analyses.

It adds explanations linking ProgPrompt's code-generation constraint and ReAct's reasoning workflow to different refusal behavior, and argues for early thought auditing over execution-stage intervention. These explanations go beyond v1's general vulnerability discussion.

However, it removes v1's manual-anchor and GPT-4o/Grok-3 instruction-generation description and promised research-only release terms. It describes SAFE-THOR as open-source without supplying a concrete project access link.

V1 Section 5.1 already reports 9,900 instructions: 1,800 basic instructions plus 8,100 augmented instructions. V3 retains this coverage under the SAFE-VERSE name.

The planning judge changes from GPT-4 to GPT-4o. It also introduces comparisons using a common GPT-4o backbone for two workflows and defense evaluations across four backbones.

E4.justification: The six-family jailbreak robustness design remains. V3 adds an intervention analysis comparing defenses and no defense on benign utility and environment-harm outcomes in Figures 7–8. Figure 5 replaces the laptop/mirror failure example with a potato/window example. Section 5.3 largely interprets existing benchmark measurements rather than adding a separate error-analysis experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Additional result rows and averages in v3 do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The earlier model results are replaced by extensive results for the revised backbones and workflows, including per-attack Appendix A.1 tables. New defense results report SAFE-AUDIT's mean environment-harm TSR of 0.48% and a 2.22-percentage-point average benign TSR increase over no defense. These are new comparisons under v3's settings, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

M1.justification: V3 adds SAFE-AUDIT, a GPT-4o-based module that examines the agent's initial thought before planning, replaces unsafe reasoning with refusal, enriches safe but suboptimal reasoning, or passes it through. Unfilled conference-template fields are visible.

These gains are tempered by lost dataset-generation details, visible template placeholders and reporting inconsistencies: for example, Qwen-VL-Plus's environment-harm PSR is 46.89% in Table 2 but 42.89% in Figure 8. No new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced. The new nearest-neighbor distance summaries describe diagnostic outcomes rather than estimation uncertainty.

The stocking-index section also newly attributes its superior performance specifically to embedding efficiency.

Previously intended releases gain concrete GEOTESSERA retrieval and integrity-checking instructions, model/code access information, and disclosure that Brazilian plot data require a Data Transfer Agreement.

Limitations now discuss transfer from pretraining distributions, model bias, temperature and sampling effects, and restricted experimental scale and domains.

(7) and KL-based top-quartile data selection in Section 5.3. The covariance approximation idea remains.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the paper into two columns, moves the teaser to the first page, redraws Figure 2 horizontally, expands Table 1, and adds a user-study table. v1 Figure 7 is retained as v2 Figure 6; v1's separate celebrity-results Figure 6 is absent. However, v2 does not clarify whether the unchanged original scores use the enlarged MotionBench, and its new ± values lack statistical definitions. Its absent appendix also prevents checking I2V comparisons, quantitative ablations, implementation details, and limitations available in v1. However, v1 includes Appendices A-C, while v2 ends after the references despite referring to an appendix for additional comparisons and quantitative ablations. It adds a Table 2 footnote clarifying trainval training for unmarked baseline rows. V2 newly references loss-weight ablations in supplementary material that is not included, so their existence, design, and extent cannot be assessed.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental results. The Gaussian-mixture distributions describe the method rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Figure 5 revises three reported mAP values: at 10% labeling, RBox-only changes from 52.48 to 52.82 and the 9:1 RBox:HBox mixture from 52.36 to 52.94; at 30%, RBox-only changes from 60.35 to 60.91. Figures 1 and 2 are extensively redesigned, the noise table is transposed, and other displays are resized and relocated. Figures 3 and 4 exchange numbering while retaining their underlying content.

R1.justification: The related-work positioning is largely retained, but bibliography entries for ReDet, Large Selective Kernel Network, Dense Teacher, ARSL, and SOOD++ are removed. The latter three remain comparison methods. Reference reordering and bibliographic formatting changes do not constitute additional substantive changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and loss/filtering equations retain their substance. Equation 8's explicit weights reduce to the previous expression at the stated values of one. No new assumptions, proofs, or substantive derivations are supplied.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the trainval footnote and refreshes the visual presentation, but removes useful preprocessing and evaluation details and introduces Figure 1's conflicting 20%-supervision performance claims. The main benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the referenced new ablations are unavailable. Within the supplied PDFs, these reporting and reproducibility losses outweigh the limited clarification and presentation gains.

A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same PWOOD work, with matching methods and experiments. Neither contains an appendix. V2 refers to supplementary hyperparameter ablations in Sections 3.2 and 3.4, but that supplement is absent, limiting comparison of those analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–5, with several revised values in Figure 5.

C2.justification: v3 adds an implicit-prior regularization explanation, interprets uncertainty caused by unstable foreground masks, and suggests a memory-locality explanation for the 1D FPS anomaly. For GaussianHeadAvatar, v3 specifies 600k iterations and a detailed multi-view protocol, whereas v1 lacks corresponding settings and reports 9–9.5 hours instead of over two days. Whether the underlying protocol changed or was newly documented cannot be reliably determined.

The Bayesian treatment adds interpretation rather than a new training objective.

The enlarged related-work table distinguishes optimization, feed-forward and pseudo-ground-truth approaches and their resource requirements. v3 also claims a unified probabilistic interpretation of earlier high-dimensional Gaussian methods.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its second integration mainly through two illustrated multi-view examples with little implementation or evaluation detail. v3 supplies aggregate ten-subject results, an NDGS control and detailed integration and data protocols, substantially strengthening the assessability and reproducibility of the broader applicability claim. The unchanged monocular evidence is preserved. Dropped limitations and unexplained dataset-count and training-time differences remain weaknesses, but the gains in empirical support and documentation outweigh them.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HyperGaussians with the same authors and core formulation. All 16 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains original monocular results and reports aggregate multi-view reconstruction results, NDGS comparisons, ablations and computational measurements.

before.justification: v1 reports original avatar reconstruction results, quantitative ablations, computational benchmarks, and appendix comparisons involving GaussianHeadAvatar and NDGS.

The revised conclusion makes an existing limitation more prominent but adds only a proposed remedy. With the methods, validation, reproducibility information and detailed appendix retained, overall paper quality remains broadly unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the central claim about content-specific query representations and attention sharing with a claim that dominant singular components of the third feature encode style, motivating PFB and SAC. Training-free personalization from a single reference and efficient autoregressive generation remain the overarching goals.

C2.justification: v2 explains style/content separation through leading versus higher-rank singular components and interprets weaker spectral decay as increasing content leakage. It also adds an explicit limitation: heterogeneous reference styles can become blended because the method cannot selectively isolate sub-styles. v1 instead emphasizes query-based content control and ends with general future directions.

D1.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1, the spectral-decay setting, and extensive baseline implementation information, including repository provenance, default configurations, the unofficial StyleDrop implementation, and a shared A6000/PyTorch environment. Table 1 and Appendix C explicitly explain that tuning-based runtimes include style-specific training plus one generated image. These substantially expand documentation without establishing that retained baseline experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The 190-prompt Parti benchmark, ten quantitative reference styles, and image-guided and text-only generation tasks remain. Qualitative artistic-style coverage changes: v2 includes geometric flat illustration, metallic 3D, neon comic art, and retro sci-fi examples, while earlier Mesopotamian-relief examples disappear. Additional backbones change model settings rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 5 add CSGO and StyleAR to the six retained external baselines. B-LoRA joins the user-study comparison. For text-only style-aligned generation, v2 Figure 14 adds comparisons against StyleAligned and AlignedGen, whereas v1 Figure 8 displays only the proposed method.

E3.justification: v2 adds the harmonic mean of prompt and style fidelity as an evaluation metric. The user study changes from 40 participants choosing among four methods to 30 choosing among five. New experiments introduce mixed object/color prompt-pair controls and evaluation on Infinity-8B and Switti. The primary Infinity-2B benchmark, output resolution, and stated GPU remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The step-wise prompt-injection analysis is retained, but the query/key/value replacement analysis is replaced by baseline, full-feature replacement, and SVD-guided controls. Component ablations are redesigned around replacement, PFB, and SAC. Appendix A adds top-k singular-component and exponential-decay sensitivity studies, and Appendix D tests qualitative generalization across backbones.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional averaged CLIP results and the revised user-study sample size do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: On the retained benchmark, Table 1 changes the proposed method's prompt fidelity from 0.330 to 0.334, style fidelity from 0.603 to 0.630, and reported runtime from 6.44 to 3.58 seconds; the six shared baselines' corresponding values remain unchanged. v2 adds baseline, harmonic-score, spectral-analysis, sensitivity, and backbone results. User preferences change from 57.5%/30.5% to 35.3%/32.0% for prompt/style fidelity, but the changed participants and candidate set preclude interpreting these as comparable gains or losses.

M1.justification: v1's three-path system uses feature initialization, Key Stage Attention Sharing at steps 2–3, and similarity-weighted Adaptive Query Sharing at steps 4–7. v2 replaces this with two generation streams conditioned on the same prompt, SVD-based Principal Feature Blending at the third feature, and Structural Attention Correction replacing content queries and keys at steps 3–12. These change the inference procedure, rather than merely renaming components.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, substantial introduction passages, mechanism analysis, method description, ablation discussion, and conclusion are rewritten around the SVD formulation. The appendix is reorganized into analysis, algorithm, implementation, backbone experiments, limitations, and qualitative-results sections. This substantially changes the narrative beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the pipeline schematic and replaces the attention-feature illustration with a spectral-analysis display. It expands the comparison table, changes the ablation-table structure and placement, adds sensitivity plots and a user-preference table, and revises qualitative grids. Typography, author presentation, references, and overall page layout also change substantially.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references including CSD-VAR, FLUX, multimodal diffusion editing, CSGO, StyleAR, and AlignedGen, and connects the revised mechanism to prior feature decomposition and attention editing. Most of the three-part related-work discussion remains. Publication updates and duplicate entries for existing works do not constitute additional research coverage.

T1.justification: The mathematical construction changes from attention concatenation and cosine-weighted query mixing to principal/residual feature decomposition, an exponentially weighted SVD operator, and residual-preserving reconstruction in v2 Section 5.2. Appendix A additionally defines top-k decompositions and interventions. These substantively revise the formal definitions; neither version provides theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence and documentation supporting its revised mechanism. Full-replacement/SVD controls, component ablations, and rank/decay sweeps provide more diagnostic support than v1's narrower attention-sharing analysis. Algorithm and baseline documentation address important reproducibility gaps, while timing clarification and explicit mixed-style limitations improve transparency. The smaller, redesigned user study cannot establish a preference improvement, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but these limits do not outweigh the substantial gains in mechanistic support and reproducibility.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same training-free style-personalization work using scale-wise autoregressive models, despite retitling and substantial methodological revision. All pages, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

after.justification: v2 reports original SVD intervention experiments, benchmark and ablation results, sensitivity analyses, a 30-participant user study, and qualitative experiments on additional backbones.

before.justification: v1 reports original prompt-injection experiments, benchmark results in Table 1, component ablations including appendix Table 2, and a 40-participant user study.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first diffusion dataset-condensation framework, consisting of Select and Attach, and substantial training acceleration with small datasets across architectures and resolutions. The headline 4.3 FID at 40k steps and 100–233× acceleration claims are retained. New supporting experiments and revised research positioning do not materially change these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1 Appendix A's explicit acknowledgment that final converged performance does not fully match baseline benchmarks, together with its proposed encoder fine-tuning remedy. It adds interpretations concerning weak or absent scorer viability, encoder robustness, expected text-to-image applicability and why medium-only selection underperforms interval sampling. These materially change the discussion of mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 adds Algorithm 2 specifying frozen-model latent encoding, noise injection and averaging of denoising losses, explains how the existing Medium selection variant is constructed, and provides scoring and training times. Figure 5 also newly specifies the backbone and absence of CFG. Core hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain substantially unchanged, with no new code or data access information.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet-1K class-to-image generation at 256×256 and 512×512. v3 adds CIFAR-10 generation and analyzes LAION text-image pairs scored with SDXL, extending both dataset and conditioning coverage. The LAION experiment reports a difficulty distribution, not trained text-to-image generation performance.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds RDED to the SRe2L comparison on both DiT-L/2 and SiT-L/2. New Table 3 adds REPA-E and REG to the acceleration comparisons and reports additional L-model comparisons with REPA. The Random, K-Center and Herding comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The existing ImageNet budgets, resolutions and documented training defaults are retained. Added experiments introduce a CIFAR-10 protocol with 100 images per class, a 1K training subset and 100k steps, plus alternative scorer and visual-encoder configurations. Recall is removed from the main evaluation description and result tables, although its definition remains in Appendix D. These are bounded protocol additions and reporting changes.

E4.justification: v3 Table 5 expands the component ablation to separate Select and Attach contributions. Tables 6 and 7 add tests of strong, weaker and absent scoring models, computational overhead and visual-encoder robustness. Figure 10 extends the condensation failure examples to RDED. Conversely, v1 Figure 7's additional interval and fixed-mean-loss sampling curves are removed; the other interval analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The added experiments do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results include RDED gFID values of 166.2 and 97.5, CIFAR-10 gFID of 9.72 for Random versus 3.95 for D2C, and additional component, encoder and runtime results. Table 1 is unchanged, and the 512×512 SiT 300k results already appeared in v1 Appendix J. Recall entries and the removed Figure 7 results disappear. New Table 3 assigns 10k steps to DiT scores 14.81 and 4.2, whereas Table 1 still assigns them 100k; these entries cannot establish a verified same-setting acceleration gain.

M1.justification: Appendix G adds a limited text-to-image adaptation that replaces class conditioning with text conditioning during difficulty scoring. The core class-to-image Select/Attach pipeline, DC-Embedding, visual alignment and training objective remain unchanged. Revisions to the conflicting score and sorting descriptions do not establish an actual redesign of the class-to-image procedure.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, scoring explanation and conclusion. It introduces a separate experimental setup subsection and reorganizes the supplementary sections. The limitations and broader-impact sections disappear, while positioning, exploration and acknowledgment sections are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column formatting, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. v3 consolidates the 512×512 results into the main table, removes Recall columns, expands ablation and baseline tables, adds a scoring algorithm and LAION histogram, and expands the condensation visualization with RDED. Most existing method diagrams and generation galleries are retained rather than newly produced.

R1.justification: The introduction, related work and new Appendix A substantially reposition D2C within image-level condensation through selection and enrichment of real images, broadening v1's synthetic-data optimization framing. New discussion distinguishes D2C from InfoBatch and Pruning then Reweighting and relates it to OD3 and other image-level approaches. References also expand to newer acceleration methods, including REG and REPA-E.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the approximate constant-denominator assumption and the mathematical difficulty-score definition. v1 Equation 6's negative-log-of-exponential expression becomes negative expected squared error in v3 Equation 7, and the stated score ordering reverses. The revised equation still conflicts with Algorithm 2's positive mean squared error. These are limited formal revisions, with no new theorem or proof.

improvement.justification: The added component controls, scorer-dependence tests and end-to-end timing analysis address important gaps in v1's efficiency evidence; RDED and CIFAR-10 results also strengthen validation. However, v3 removes Recall results exposing diversity tradeoffs and the explicit final-convergence limitation. Its new acceleration table also introduces conflicting 10k versus 100k training budgets for identical DiT scores. E3.justification: FID is replaced by ImageReward, and new artifact-rate and edge-energy evaluations are introduced. The FLUX 4× configuration with 18 RALU steps is replaced by a 5× configuration with 15 steps. New protocols include 100-image artifact analyses, four-step distilled-model integrations, and A6000 benchmarking. The retained FLUX 7× and SD3 stage counts merely change from per-stage to cumulative notation.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends v2's qualitative upsampling-timing study and limited parameter ablations with systematic timing/JSD analyses, artifact rate versus FLOPs, and quantitative ratio sweeps. Appendix C adds image-space versus latent-space edge detection, fixed versus adaptive selection, interpolation comparisons, and edge-mask visualizations. These directly test previously unsupported design choices.

E5.justification: v3 adds error bars in Figures 2–3, a p < 0.001 statement for the ImageReward/JSD relationship, and FLOP mean±standard deviation in Table S4. GenEval reporting changes from fixed-seed wording to four different seeds per prompt. The error-bar definition and significance-test procedure remain unspecified; the wording does not establish increased repeated runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds or replaces extensive results, including ImageReward scores, expanded comparisons, distilled-model integrations, hardware measurements, and artifact ablations. For retained FLUX 7× RALU, reported latency changes from 3.37 to 3.75 seconds, while NIQE 6.87 and CLIP-IQA 0.681 remain unchanged. T2I-CompBench/GenEval change from 0.566/0.646 to 0.633/0.682 under revised task coverage, so these are not established same-setting gains.

M1.justification: The core procedure remains low-resolution denoising, selective early upsampling using decoded Canny edges, and full-resolution refinement, with correlated noise and JSD-based timestep matching. NT-DM becomes NT-Matching, but its underlying algorithm remains equivalent. Additional positional-embedding explanations and experiments with other acceleration methods do not establish a changed RALU algorithm.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, artifact discussion, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. NT-DM is renamed NT-Matching, experiments gain dedicated artifact and edge-selection sections, and a Discussion section is introduced. Appendices are reorganized and references move after them, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 switches to a two-column layout, redraws the framework diagram, merges the main benchmark tables, restructures integration displays, and adds quantitative artifact plots and appendix tables. Qualitative comparison panels and captions are revised. Some SD3 and FLUX 7× appendix images are retained and relocated, rather than newly added results.

R1.justification: v3 adds context on Latent-SR and image-space super-resolution, forecasting methods, and token merging, alongside references supporting new metrics and implementations. FID and VQ4DiT references are removed. These additions refine the positioning, while the central distinction from training-dependent approaches and Bottleneck Sampling remains.

T1.justification: v3 Eqs. (5)–(6) correct the main-text matching target to a latent with isotropic covariance, replacing v2 Eq. (5)'s upsampled-latent target. Appendix A.1 adds consequences for intermediate and fully denoised endpoints. The rescheduling formulas otherwise remain equivalent, and the appendix's inconsistent covariance expressions in Eqs. (S2) and (S4) persist.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence for the central artifact-mitigation claims through controlled analyses and design-choice ablations, addressing v2's reliance on mostly qualitative artifact examples. Broader competitive baselines, integration tests, and execution details also improve assessment and reproducibility. FID removal and changed task subsets limit direct score comparisons, and reporting inconsistencies remain, such as FLUX 7× NIQE being 6.87 in Table 1 but 6.51 in Table 3. These shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RALU research despite different titles and extensive reformatting. All 28 pages of v2 and 29 pages of v3, including appendices A–E, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures for comparison.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, controlled artifact analyses, design ablations, hardware measurements, and integrations with temporal acceleration and distilled models.

before.justification: v2 reports original RALU experiments on FLUX and SD3, including quantitative comparisons, caching integration, ablations, and generated images in the appendices.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same three contributions: dual-direction geometric representation, the HV Fusion Module, and a dataset with horizontal/vertical annotations. Claims of improved document flatness, readability, and state-of-the-art performance remain. The abstract's explicit mention of three benchmarks reflects coverage already present in v1.

C2.justification: v3 explains text-sparse difficulties through weaker line guidance, replacing v1's emphasis on difficult figure/table boundary detection. It expands the Chinese-document discussion with a proposed convolutional alternative and its computational cost, adds a speed-quality interpretation, and suggests foreground/UV information for background interference. The explicit irregular-boundary failure qualification is removed.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies pooled feature dimensions and deformation-field channels, and newly documents equal-count self-attention controls for existing ablations. Its abstract changes promised release to stated availability at the D2Dewarp repository, although future-release wording remains elsewhere; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Existing training hyperparameters and software versions are retained.

E2.justification: The quantitative comparator sets are substantially reduced. Table II to Table 2 removes DocUNet, FCN-based, Piece-Wise, DocTr, DDCP, FDRNet, and DocTr-Plus, while adding DvD. DIR300 loses DocProj, DewarpNet, DocTr, DDCP, and DocRes; DocReal loses DocTr, DDCP, FTDR, and DocRes. Some removed quantitative comparators remain in qualitative figures.

It also introduces parameter-count and per-image runtime comparisons. The proposed model's training settings, benchmark sizes, OCR subsets, and accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations retain their results. v3 adds a training-data control, a focused horizontal-rectification comparison in Figure 5, and a text-dense/text-sparse illustration in Figure 6. It removes the unclear-boundary failure example from v1 Figure 8 while retaining the background-text failure case.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-training run counts, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. The newly reported average processing time does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The reported result set changes substantially through comparator-row removals, new DvD and retrained DocScanner scores, parameter counts, and runtime results. DocReal's distorted-input AD/ED/CER change from 0.771/1500.56/0.5234 to 0.969/333.52/0.4432. DocTLNet's DIR300 CER changes from 0.1767 to 0.178, beyond equivalent rounding. D2Dewarp's benchmark and component-ablation scores remain unchanged apart from rounding.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, dual line decoders, pooling and attention fusion, deformation-field prediction, and training-loss equations remain unchanged. Added pooling/output descriptions clarify the existing method. Convolutional downsampling is discussed as a possible enhancement, without establishing its adoption.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, result discussions, limitations, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting and condensation. Related work gains thematic subdivisions, and ablations become part of the experimental-results subsection. The title, author order, and affiliation presentation also change, while much of the core method description is retained.

Qualitative panels are reduced or replaced, including removal of the separate DIR300 and DocReal comparison grids and addition of a local-crop comparison. Tables add a parameter column and consolidate metric columns.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including DocMamba, DocMatcher, DvD, and document enhancement/evaluation work, while removing DocProj, FDRNet, and several peripheral recognition references. It drops the explicit acknowledgment of RDGR's rule-based vertical information. The central positioning around complementary horizontal/vertical features remains.

Other mathematical expressions are equivalent; removal of the expanded standard BCE formulas does not constitute a substantive theoretical change.

improvement.justification: The same-training-data DocScanner comparison in Tables 2-3 addresses a confound left open in v1, while clearer fusion diagrams, disclosed ablation controls, and resource reporting improve interpretability. These gains are limited by reduced comparison and failure-case coverage, unspecified timing conditions, and the new Equation 4 indexing inconsistency. The central method and its performance evidence remain stable, supporting a modest overall improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe D2Dewarp and DocDewarpHV. All 10 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v3 were inspected, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Tables II-IV report original dewarping and OCR evaluations on DocUNet, DIR300, and DocReal; Tables V-VI report component ablations.

The scalability limitation changes from handling large-scale scenes to handling long videos; reconstruction-quality and external-camera-estimation limitations are retained.

Appendix A.2 revises final-stage sampling from the previously described 13-frame, 518×518 setting to 2–13 frames and aspect ratios 0.5–2, although A.3 retains the fixed-setting wording. A.1 also adds Depth Pro to preprocessing. These reported changes do not establish that retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

Figure S.1 replaces v1 Figure 6's reconstruction examples with new DAVIS results. Tables 2–6 retain their results; multiplying SSIM values by 100 is a reporting-scale change, not improved performance.

M1.justification: Both retain dynamic splatter pixels, the VGGT-based backbone, depth and splatter heads, a time-conditioned motion head, and depth/rendering/motion objectives. Added loss specifications and initialization details document the existing approach; the scratch-initialized configuration is an ablation, not a replacement method.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose, merges the dynamic-reconstruction and dynamic-view-synthesis related-work subsections, reorganizes the appendix discussion, licensing, and visualization sections, and adds Tao Hu to the author list. The main introduction–method–experiments–conclusion narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: The paper and textual appendices change from single-column to two-column layout. Figures 1–2 are substantially redrawn, tables and figures are relocated, and Table 1 is shortened while its full information is retained in Table S.1. The former reconstruction panel is replaced by a four-column DAVIS visualization, and supplementary captions are expanded.

R1.justification: v2 adds STORM and DAVIS citations and removes several static-reconstruction references, including MoGe, Fast3R, and MASt3R-SLAM. Related work newly distinguishes STORM's multi-view outdoor-driving setting and drops the detailed DynaDUSt3R discussion. The main positioning relative to BTimer and NutWorld remains.

T1.justification: New Equations 3–4 formally specify the previously prose-described depth and rendering objectives, including an L1 gradient penalty and weighted LPIPS term. The unsquared L2 notation leaves an inconsistency with the retained MSE description. Existing deformation and motion-loss mathematics remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

improvement.justification: Explicit loss weights, initialization and sampling details, and clearer visualization provenance improve reproducibility and interpretation. DAVIS examples and the initialization experiment provide useful additional evidence without changing the central benchmark findings. These gains are limited by the unsupported claim of comparable scratch-training outcomes and inconsistencies in the new loss notation and final-stage training description. Overall, the added transparency and evidence provide a modest quality improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoVieS work and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched across the substantial reformatting and supplementary-material renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view-synthesis and 3D-point-tracking results, quantitative ablations in Tables 4–6, and qualitative reconstruction, flow, and segmentation results.

Its introduction also newly claims standalone LLaVA LaSM reaches 100%, which conflicts with v2 Table 1.

Sections 8.2 and 8.4–8.6 add substantive discussion of controlled CoT evaluation, benign pop-ups, the DSR–TSR gap and failure mechanisms. Conversely, v1's explicit limitations concerning preliminary interpretability and lack of physical-device evaluation are omitted.

Section 9.3 newly explains OS-Atlas official action/coordinate prompting and target-region scoring. These improve documented reproducibility information without establishing changes to all previously evaluated settings.

E1.justification: Both retain 200 base screenshots expanded into 2,400 perturbations and the AndroidControl evaluation of 224 episodes. V2 adds explicit spatial variation through top, middle and bottom pop-up conditions in Section 8.5. The multi-step task itself already appeared in v1 Appendix B.3.

E2.justification: The standalone comparator set remains No Defense, DPO, Direct Alert and CoT Alert. V2 Table 1 additionally reports DPO+LaSM and Direct Alert+LaSM combinations; v1 Tables 1–2 reported LaSM alone and CoT+LaSM but lacked those two combinations.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation configurations through two additional backbones, GELab-Zero-4B and MAI-UI-8B, a denser two-model coefficient sweep and controlled position tests. It also changes the stated Type metric from typing accuracy to action-type exact match. FESR becomes TSR with the same episode-success meaning, and the original 224-episode construction remains.

E4.justification: V2 expands the four-value coefficient analysis into a two-model sweep, adds controlled position robustness tests and presents two failure modes involving minimal interfaces and text input. The original component ablation and hidden-state analysis remain; v1 Figure 7 is relocated as v2 Figure 12 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both provide point estimates and sample averages. V2 Table 1's arrows describe performance differences after applying LaSM, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Central results are extensively replaced. Qwen overlay averages for No Defense/LaSM change from 39.3/74.8 in v1 Table 1 to 18.9/66.4 in v2 Table 1. LLaVA CoT+LaSM overlay/inductive averages change from 100/100 to 86.9/90.3. V2 also adds combination, backbone, coefficient and position results. These are reported result replacements, not established same-setting performance changes, because the versions do not fully reconcile their experimental conditions.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same joint attention/MLP parameter scaling, Equation 3 and progressive layer-range narrowing. The added coefficient-selection discussion elaborates hyperparameter tuning; it does not establish a different defense mechanism.

P1.justification: The introduction and main-results narrative are substantially rewritten, Section 6 is reorganized, and supplementary discussion precedes implementation details instead of following them. The hidden-state discussion moves from the main text to Section 8.7. Author information and acknowledgments also expand.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and merges the two main result tables into a combined table with baseline, post-LaSM and difference values. Heatmap and screenshot examples are replaced or redesigned, new coefficient/position/failure displays are added, and existing prompt boxes become separately captioned full-page figures.

R1.justification: V2 adds three cited works: LLM for Mobile, the OS Agents survey and Agent-ScanKit. The latter supports a new connection between failure cases and memorization versus reasoning. The existing GUI-agent, injection-attack and saliency-method positioning otherwise remains substantially intact.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same attention-patch, cosine-similarity, scaling-update and attention-averaging mathematics. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs. The revised empirical Type metric does not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

improvement.justification: The added position tests, failure analyses, coefficient studies and code link improve evidence and usability. However, v2 introduces material reporting conflicts: its introduction claims standalone LLaVA achieves 100%, whereas Table 1 reports averages of 81.2% and 78.0%; Section 6.2 retains DPO's v1 score of 1.42%, while Table 1 reports 52.3%. The unexplained replacement of central results and omission of the physical-device limitation counterbalance the useful additions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LaSM. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised and added content despite substantial reformatting.

after.justification: Sections 5–6 and supplementary Sections 8–9 report original defense evaluations, including backbone comparisons, coefficient sweeps, position tests and failure analyses.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix B.3 report original defense evaluations, scaling ablations and AndroidControl episode results.

C1.justification: The central adaptive-width and Token Recycling contributions, including the headline 2.0/2.9 percentage-point ImageNet claims, remain unchanged. v2 adds explicit main-text claims of demonstrated segmentation and Swin transfer and superiority to depth-adaptive methods. These refine and extend applicability claims whose broader architectural motivation already appeared in v1.

C2.justification: v1 Section 4.5 presents uniformly hard inputs as an efficiency limitation; v2 Section 4.8 recasts the retained evidence as successful routing and continued superiority, dropping the explicit efficiency warning. The discussion of hierarchical token-alignment difficulties is also removed. v2 adds interpretations of segmentation refinement and demonstrated pruning complementarity, while retaining training-overhead and excessive-expansion limitations in Appendix I.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies inference batch size 512, validation-set throughput aggregation, GMAC accounting, and filtering/rebatching pseudocode in Appendix J. It also documents Swin stage allocation and the pruning ratio. Reported training hardware changes from A100 to H100, without establishing reruns of retained results. Code access is unchanged, and detailed training settings for the new applications remain sparse.

E1.justification: v2 adds semantic segmentation on ADE20K and Cityscapes, extending evaluation beyond ImageNet-family classification to dense prediction and urban scenes. The existing ImageNet variants remain covered. Swin is an architectural extension, while DETR remains future work rather than evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 8 adds Swin-T/S/B comparisons and six early-exit comparators: SDN, PABEE, BERxiT, ViT-EE, PCEE, and LGViT. Figure 14 adds A-ViT and AdaViT; Figure 9 compares Segmenter backbones. The depth-expanded controls in v1 Table 1 disappear. The earlier appendix Early Exit baseline is retained under the name BranchyNet, with unchanged results.

E3.justification: New segmentation evaluations introduce mIoU under single-scale and multi-scale inference with a linear Segmenter decoder, while the new early-exit comparison uses Swin backbones. The DynamicViT combination specifies a 0.8 pruning ratio. v2 also exempts the new KV-cache experiment from the retained ablations' stochastic-training setup. These are added experimental settings, not evidence that retained ImageNet experiments were rerun.

It removes the depth-expansion control in Table 1. Existing head-expansion, loss-weighting, fusion, entropy, and prediction-dynamics analyses largely remain; moving the head-expansion analyses to Appendix K does not make them new.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the results. The statement about roughly 100 prototyping runs remains unchanged. Prediction entropy is a routing signal, not newly added statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds segmentation, Swin, early-exit, and pruning-combination results. Section 4.6 reports 83.5% accuracy at 9.5 GMACs for the Swin adaptation, and Table 4 adds KV-cache accuracies of 73.872% and 75.674% across rounds. Table 1 changes the one-extra-iteration cost from 3.45 to 2.5 GMACs and removes depth-expanded results. Most retained ImageNet results, including the entropy-threshold table, are unchanged.

M1.justification: The core nested subnetworks, Token Recycling, joint losses, and entropy-based stopping remain unchanged. v2 adds a Swin-S adaptation that keeps the first architectural stage intact while initially halving the other stages, and an optional DynamicViT pruning component in the second inference round. The batching pseudocode documents inference rather than establishing a changed core algorithm.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, method overview, hard-input discussion, and conclusion around a broader application narrative. It removes the isomorphic-architecture subsection, reorganizes evaluation and appendices, and moves head-expansion/loss-weighting explanations into Appendix K. These are substantial structural and narrative revisions alongside the added scientific content.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a predominantly single-column layout to two columns, swaps the opening performance and architecture figures, merges ImageNet comparison panels, and splits other appendix panels. Ablation tables move into the supplement. New Swin, segmentation, and qualitative figures, expanded pruning plots, and batching pseudocode substantially change the visual presentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantial early-exit discussion distinguishing adaptive depth from ThinkingViT's progressive width, covering methods such as MSDNet, SDN, PABEE, BERxiT, LGViT, and JEI-DNN. It adds references supporting segmentation, Swin, A-ViT, and AdaViT, while removing works including Once-for-All, LLaMaFlex, MatMamba, and Sliced Recursive Transformer. This expands research positioning beyond bibliographic reformatting.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of nesting, token fusion, joint training, and entropy stopping is retained, with equation splitting and renumbering. v2's weighted-average GMACs formula explains the existing compute metric; it does not introduce a new theoretical result. Neither version supplies substantive theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: The segmentation and Swin experiments provide substantial empirical support for portability claims that v1 largely left untested. Broader early-exit comparisons address an important alternative to progressive width, while pruning integration and inference-measurement details strengthen practical validation. These gains outweigh sparse settings for the new experiments and the less explicit treatment of the hard-input efficiency limitation; the improvement comes from stronger validation, not higher retained ImageNet scores.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ThinkingViT and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained experiments can be matched across substantial reformatting, renumbering, and relocation.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification experiments and reports additional segmentation, Swin, early-exit comparison, and token-reuse/pruning results.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet classification, throughput, robustness, routing, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

These are additional benchmark results, not same-setting improvements over v2.

improvement.justification: The ImageNet-21K experiment supplies useful evidence for broader classification scalability, and the Table 3 correction makes routing usage consistent with the reported GMACs. These strengthen empirical support and internal consistency. The gains are limited by unchanged core evidence and an unresolved reporting ambiguity: Appendix J's new 20-minute epoch time is not reconciled with Section 4.1's retained 10-minute figure on two GPUs.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ThinkingViT. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including content moved or renumbered in v3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds ImageNet-21K experiments in Appendix I.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, semantic segmentation, efficiency, robustness, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: physically guided side-view synthesis, progressive multi-view refinement, and efficient smoke reconstruction supporting re-simulation. C1.justification: The second introduction contribution shifts from introducing CIL and CDAP to an efficient adaptation scheme combining lightweight adapters and learnable tokens. The central image-adaptive generalization claim and headline state-of-the-art performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets its new Grad-CAM comparison as improved attention to forgery-related regions versus irrelevant baseline attention; v1 emphasized semantic regions across different views. It also adds capacity/efficiency explanations for N_t selection and the effectiveness/efficiency tradeoff behind two tuning steps.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents the 1024-dimensional encoder features and channel-wise gating coefficients. Existing hardware, optimizer, training budget, token counts and test-time tuning defaults remain consistent. The code destination is unchanged, now presented through a hyperlink.

E1.justification: Both versions train on ProGAN for UniversalFakeDetect and SD v1.4 for GenImage, evaluating the same 19 and eight subsets respectively. The additional ablations and visual examples remain within existing coverage.

E2.justification: UniversalFakeDetect Tables 1-2 remove CNN-Spot, Patchfor and Co-occurence. GenImage Table 3 removes Spec, CNN-Spot, F3Net and GramNet. The remaining comparison methods, including the strongest reported competitors, are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds experiments varying N_t over 3, 6, 9 and 12 and tuning steps over 1, 2 and 3, plus separate real/fake accuracy reporting. The main benchmark protocols and default settings remain unchanged. N_t is inconsistently called a token count despite its earlier definition as a prompted-layer endpoint.

E4.justification: V2 adds N_t and tuning-step sensitivity studies and separates the gating contribution in its revised component ablation. Figure 5 replaces the cross-view Grad-CAM example with comparisons without and with IAPL. Adapter-placement and UniversalFakeDetect entropy-loss analyses are retained, while the GenImage entropy-loss ablation is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Prediction-confidence selection is retained and does not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All shared entries in Tables 1-3 are unchanged, including IAPL's 95.61% UniversalFakeDetect mAcc, 99.32% mAP and 96.7% GenImage mAcc. V2 adds or replaces supporting results, including tuning-step accuracies of 94.47%, 94.88% and 94.94%, class-specific accuracies and new Grad-CAM findings. Removed comparator and GenImage loss-ablation entries also reduce reported results.

M1.justification: The documented pipeline retains MLP adapters, two conditional branches, gated prompt propagation, confidence-selected entropy minimization and highest-confidence view selection. Renaming shallow tokens as test-time adaptive tokens and reorganizing CDAP into token tuning and separate view selection do not establish a procedural change.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 changes from training/testing organization to Overview, Fixed Learned Parameters, Image-Adaptive Prompt Learning and Optimal View Selection, with revised terminology and expanded explanations of parameter roles.

P2.justification: V2 adds a conceptual Figure 1, redraws the architecture diagrams, relocates the retained t-SNE visualization and replaces the Grad-CAM exhibit. Ablation tables are split and restructured, while captions, highlighting, typography and page layout are substantially reformatted.

R1.justification: V2 adds related-work discussion and citations for LAA-Net and Effort, while removing references associated with Patchfor, Co-occurence and GramNet. These are limited updates; the overall positioning against static adaptation and existing prompt-learning methods remains stable.

T1.justification: The confidence score, entropy objectives and additive gated prompt updates retain their mathematical substance, with reordered equations and consolidated notation. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies fixed versus adaptive parameter roles and adds useful component controls, class-specific results and sensitivity analyses supporting design choices. The main benchmark evidence remains unchanged, with strong comparators retained. Removing the GenImage entropy-loss check and introducing inconsistent N_t terminology and a stale entropy-table reference limit the gains, but the added analysis and clearer organization support a modest overall improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IAPL study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and references throughout. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; v1 refers to supplementary material that is not included.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark evaluations and reports additional ablation results, parameter sweeps and comparative attention visualizations.

before.justification: V1 reports original IAPL evaluations on UniversalFakeDetect and GenImage, component ablations, and feature and attention visualizations.

R1.justification: V3 adds ATTSD, MiraGe and Frank et al.'s frequency-analysis work, and removes references associated with Spec, F3Net and DeiT-S. MiraGe also enters the introduction's comparison with fixed prompts. The broader positioning around CLIP adaptation and prompt learning remains intact.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same fusion, confidence and entropy definitions. Changes to condition subscripts and layer-index notation are equivalent notation; no assumptions, theoretical results or proofs are added.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the existing evidence easier to assess through explicit SAFE evaluation provenance, updated comparators, class-specific ablation results and corrected labels and references. The benefit is limited by the overbroad Table 6 interpretation and unavailable referenced supplementary material; the method and headline results remain unchanged.

A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same IAPL study, with corresponding equations, five figures and nine tables. Neither contains an appendix. V3 references separate supplementary details and experiments that are not supplied; no changes in that material can be inferred.

The scientific evidence is unchanged, and removing supplementary pointers does not resolve the missing detailed CNN architecture description, so the overall gain is limited.

T1.justification: Equations 1-4 retain the same forward/reverse diffusion definitions and training objectives. Neither version adds or revises a formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves evaluation transparency by specifying score aggregation in Section 5.2 and makes existing VQA examples accessible beside the main results. A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLaDA-MedV and provide complete, readable main text and Appendices A-B. Equations, tables, figures, and examples can be matched despite relocation and formatting changes.

C1.justification: Both versions claim fine-grained diffusion-based DSSIM localization, improved detection through feature fusion, and state-of-the-art performance with greater explainability. V2's joint-task title and artifact encoder/decoder framing recast the same contributions without establishing a new capability or broader scientific claim.

C2.justification: Sections 8.3–8.4 add an explanation of the previously reported training collapse through all-black outputs and explicitly acknowledge slow inference and inapplicability to entirely synthesized images. V2 also replaces v1's multi-metric quality/efficiency tradeoff for T=50 with a task-specific explanation of its SSIM optimum.

D1.justification: Section 6.4 newly discloses ConvNeXt-B pretraining: 200 epochs, AdamW, batch size 64, learning rate 5e-5 and linear decay from epoch 100. These are additional disclosures, not established setting changes. Conversely, Figure 3 replaces the explicit GAP/Norm/Linear classifier details with a generic Head.

E1.justification: The same FF++, CDF2, DFDC, DFDCP and FFIW datasets remain. V2 adds controlled JPEG compression, occlusion, Gaussian noise and blur scenarios on CDF2, extending input-condition coverage without introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces LESB with reproduced Effort results; the other main benchmark comparators remain. V2 additionally compares against SBI in the new corruption experiment and against DDIM in the sampling analysis.

E3.justification: Main benchmark protocols remain unchanged. V2 specifies three severity levels per corruption and replaces the timestep study at T=40/50/75/100 with DDPM evaluations at T=20/50/100/500/1000 and DDIM sampling budgets using a T=1000 model. This study now reports SSIM alone instead of four localization metrics.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends the analyses with a four-degradation robustness study (Figure 7), qualitative DFDC localization comparisons (Figure 8), and a broader timestep study including DDIM (Figure 9). These address additional robustness and sampling-design questions. Existing architecture, fusion, detector, seed and two-stage training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The same qualitative comparison across three denoising seeds remains, moving from v1 Figure 7 to v2 Figure 10. V2 adds no repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Substantial new corruption, sampling and DFDC qualitative results accompany unchanged main DiffusionFF scores and Tables 2–7. Effort's added results narrow the reported lead to 0.27 AUC points on DFDC and 0.03 on FFIW. Figure 7 newly reports, for example, 74.86% versus SBI's 57.10% under severe occlusion. Figure 9 reports a T=20 result despite v1 stating non-convergence for T<=30; the earlier four-metric timestep results are partly removed.

M1.justification: The pretrained detector, multi-scale U-Net conditioning, gated fusion and two-stage MSE/CE training remain unchanged. The encoder/decoder terminology and Equation 5 describe the existing design. The DDPM equation correction does not establish a change to the implemented method.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation and method explanations are extensively rewritten around joint detection/localization and artifact encoder/decoder terminology. V2 introduces a detailed numbered section hierarchy, reorganizes the analyses and supplement, and revises the title and author information.

P2.justification: V2 extensively reformats the title block, typography, table captions and placement of figures and tables. It adds robustness and DFDC visualizations, replaces the timestep table with DDPM/DDIM plots, and simplifies the architecture diagram's classifier display. Existing seed examples and training-strategy results are relocated and renumbered.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Effort, DDIM, WMamba and UCF, while removing LESB. It also removes v1's criticisms that DiffForensics overuses diffusion and DiffusionFake struggles with unseen identities, instead positioning fine-grained artifact localization as an underexplored application. The overall research positioning remains similar.

T1.justification: Equation 4 is mathematically corrected: v1's deterministic clean-sample rescaling becomes a DDPM reverse update with different coefficients and an explicit Gaussian variance term. V2 also defines the noise-schedule quantities explicitly. No theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through corruption and sampling comparisons, corrects the DDPM equation, and improves reproducibility and scope clarity through pretraining details and explicit limitations. These gains are moderated by replacing v1's multi-metric timestep evidence with SSIM alone and leaving the new T=20 result inconsistent with v1's non-convergence statement. The net improvement is useful but limited.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffusionFF study and include readable supplementary material. Their methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite extensive rewriting and reformatting.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds corruption tests, DFDC localization examples and DDPM/DDIM sampling comparisons.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection and DSSIM localization results, architectural ablations and supplementary training experiments.

C1.justification: v2 adds effective, data-efficient active view selection as a principal contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, including a state-of-the-art AVS claim. The RGB/depth uncertainty and cross-scene generalization claims remain, while v1's explicit claim to the first uncertainty models providing out-of-scene generalization is removed.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses connecting LF transfer difficulties to inconsistent depth scales and directional benefits to view-dependent color effects, while removing detailed per-scene failure discussion. Some revised interpretations overstate retained evidence: the universal claim of single-view object-centric correlations above 0.8 conflicts with Table 3's TUM PRIMU values of 0.756 for rendering and 0.745 for depth.

D1.justification: v2 documents AVS initialization and training schedules and clarifies the existing CNN learning-rate decay from 0.001 to 0.00001. Most original feature and CNN settings remain. It omits the named TUM ablation subset and removes v1's code-availability sentence containing a placeholder URL; this does not establish a change in actual code availability.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates uncertainty estimation on four LF and eleven TUM scenes. v2 retains these and adds nine MipNeRF360 scenes and eight front-facing LLFF scenes for rendering uncertainty, substantially broadening scene coverage. It also introduces the active-view-selection task on MipNeRF360.

E2.justification: v1 compares against FisherRF and regression-FisherRF. v2 additionally evaluates manifold and var3DGS for rendering uncertainty, and BayesRays and manifold for depth uncertainty. Its new AVS comparison includes FisherRF, manifold, and a controlled manifold variant using the selected views with vanilla GS. The original scene-separation comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an AVS protocol reserving every eighth view for evaluation, starting from four views, and selecting up to twenty with specified iteration intervals and a 5000-iteration spherical-harmonics schedule. It also reports PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS alongside uncertainty metrics. The feature-selection removal criterion is worded oppositely to v1, although retained plots and scores do not establish that this experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The feature-selection, scene-separation, and CNN receptive-field studies are retained; the CNN study moves to Appendix E. v2 extends cross-scene analysis to background regions, adds qualitative comparisons against additional baselines, and introduces the manifold AVS control to distinguish view-selection effects from rendering-pipeline effects. These extend the existing analytical suite.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The averaged feature-selection curves and shaded variability bands are retained from v1 Figure 2 in v2 Figure 4; additional result tables do not introduce a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark, reconstruction-quality, AVS, AUSE, and background-transfer results. For example, its new AVS Table 6 reports PSNR 20.721 for PRIMU-AVS, 20.392 for FisherRF, and 20.102 for manifold with vanilla GS. Matched LF/TUM scene-separation and full-scene/object-centric transfer Pearson scores remain unchanged. Detailed per-scene results in v1 Tables 5–14 are removed, with dataset-level summaries retained.

M1.justification: The original feature construction and regression framework remain essentially unchanged. However, v2 adds PRIMU-AVS: it renders a direction-dependent coverage map with max aggregation and omitted opacity, selects the candidate view with lowest mean coverage, and iteratively adds training views without an uncertainty regressor. This substantially extends the proposed procedure.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The method is named PRIMU, visibility terminology becomes coverage, and the experiments are reorganized around general uncertainty comparisons, scene separation, and AVS. Cross-scene generalization and spatial-interaction material move into reorganized appendices; author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds comparative image grids and benchmark/AVS tables, consolidates earlier tables into different summary structures, and removes detailed per-scene tables. The workflow diagram gains an explicit regression block, and existing qualitative panels are reordered. The introductory example reuses earlier Teddy2 outputs, while the unchanged CNN plots move from v1 Figure 3 to v2 Figure 5.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around Bayesian and stochastic radiance-field uncertainty, adding discussion of BayesRays, ProvNeRF, var3DGS, and manifold. A new AVS subsection contrasts coverage-based selection with uncertainty and information-gain approaches, including ActiveNeRF and progressive camera placement. Conversely, v1's cited lineage of prediction-quality regression in detection and segmentation is removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical constructions in Equations 1–9 and the CNN kernel-family specification in Equation 10 remain equivalent. Renaming visibility as coverage and rewriting explanations do not establish a theoretical change. Neither version contains a theorem or proof, and the AVS addition is procedural rather than a new theoretical analysis.

improvement.justification: v1's state-of-the-art claim was evaluated only against FisherRF and its regression variant on LF/TUM. v2 substantially strengthens comparative validation with additional GS/NeRF baselines, broader scene coverage, reconstruction-quality context, and an AVS experiment controlling for manifold's different rendering pipeline. Removing per-scene tables and introducing misleading single-view claims and ambiguous feature-selection wording reduce transparency and precision, but the stronger comparative evidence provides a substantial net improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian-splatting uncertainty framework, renamed PRIMU in v2. The text, equations, tables, figures, and supplied appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

after.justification: v2 retains original LF/TUM experiments and reports additional uncertainty comparisons on MipNeRF360 and LLFF, plus active-view-selection results in Table 6.

before.justification: v1 reports original LF/TUM uncertainty-estimation experiments, feature-selection ablations, cross-scene generalization results, and CNN spatial-interaction experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

Causal token rewards remain the central mitigation contribution, but the main explanatory claim is substantially redefined.

C2.justification: v2 develops new interpretations linking gradient saliency, outcome-only reinforcement, and decoding to background-driven hallucination, and interprets new experiments as supporting transfer across GRPO variants. Its efficiency conclusion changes from reduced training time to an acceptable performance-cost balance. The limitations discussion drops v1's qualifications concerning deployment scenarios, static datasets, and alternative RL algorithms, retaining primarily the model-scale limitation.

E1.justification: MMBench evaluation is removed, while the new diagnostic study adds text-only descriptions as counterparts to image-question inputs. The high-resolution, grounding, and mathematics benchmarks were already evaluated in v1's appendix. v2 additionally lists ArxivQA and ThinkLite-VL as experimental datasets, but does not specify their experimental roles sufficiently to establish a distinct new training or evaluation setting.

The appendix decoding comparison replaces DeepEyes with DeCo, HA-DPO, and GCPO, while new experiments compare DAPO, Dr. GRPO, and GCPO with and without COPO. The training-efficiency comparison also replaces its comparator set.

Reward weights change from 0.5/0.5 with eta=0.3 to independently tuned 0.35/0.35, with revised sensitivity sweeps. The principal CHAIR, POPE, and GPT-4o evaluation sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds gradient-saliency comparisons between multimodal and text-only models and between models with and without COPO. Appendix H adds GRPO-variant transfer, full-sequence versus reasoning-only reward placement, and continuation-count sensitivity analyses. Existing component, decoding, and efficiency analyses are revised, while several omission/fabrication examples are replaced.

E5.justification: v2 introduces averaging over H stochastic continuations to estimate causal sufficiency, explicitly addressing decoding variability and selecting H=8. This changes statistical estimation within reward construction; it does not establish repeated independent training runs. Neither version reports benchmark confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or seed-based variability.

E6.justification: Proposed-method results change extensively: LLaVA-1.5 CHAIR_S/CHAIR_I changes from 35.5/10.5 to 19.8/5.3, and POPE from 87.0 to 88.0. These are results for revised methods/settings, limiting attribution as controlled performance improvements.

M1.justification: v2 replaces single-continuation, correct-prefix-gated sufficiency with reward-gain estimation averaged over H continuations, and replaces optimized perturbation-based necessity with the reward drop caused by masking. It adds causal rewards directly to outcome-based GRPO advantages for reasoning tokens, replacing cumulative standardized rewards with an eta coefficient. The objective also gains trajectory-length normalization. These are substantive algorithm changes beyond the COPO renaming.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and named COPO, with extensive rewrites of the abstract, introduction, problem formulation, and causal discussion. v2 introduces a dedicated empirical-analysis subsection, reorganizes method exposition, and adds numbered sections and lettered appendices. P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening illustration, adds saliency panels and a framework diagram, and incorporates the earlier dog/frisbee example into redesigned Figure 4. It merges the CHAIR and POPE tables, separates GPT evaluation from the former combined table, displays MME as a bar chart, and adds appendix tables and plots. Typography, headings, captions, and supplementary-material layout are also extensively revised.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts from general data-centric/model-centric hallucination mitigation toward reasoning post-training and limitations of GRPO. v2 adds substantial discussion and citations concerning RL, preference optimization, GCPO, and other newly evaluated methods, and revises its description of DeCo. The earlier comparison with causal chain-of-thought work remains, so it is not a new positioning element.

T1.justification: Although the SCM and PNS definition are retained, the operational mathematical definitions of sufficiency, necessity, and advantage are substantially revised. In particular, necessity becomes an explicit reward difference under removal rather than the reward of the perturbed answer, changing its mathematical relationship to indispensability. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens formulation and validation: the necessity reward now measures damage from masking, correcting v1's mismatch between its formula and claimed indispensability, while relevant preference/RL baselines and transfer and reward-placement controls address important empirical gaps. These gains outweigh the shortened limitations discussion and a new Algorithm 1 inconsistency that uses the same prefix for both sufficiency branches. The saliency evidence remains qualitative, and benchmark uncertainty is still unreported; higher scores alone do not drive this assessment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same causal sufficiency/necessity-guided GRPO research, renamed COPO in v2. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support comparison despite substantial revision.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, gradient-saliency experiments, ablations, and additional comparisons across GRPO variants and reward-placement implementations.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, parameter sensitivity, qualitative examples, and decoding comparisons in the main text and appendix.

It also adds explanations of failures caused by overly constrained video-generation prompts.

These are documentation changes in addition to the actual protocol revisions; the project-page access information remains unchanged.
