C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit contribution claim of negligible or minimal additional inference overhead in the abstract and introduction. The central claims concerning reward optimization, generalization, composability and mitigation of reward hacking remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations attributing prompt-length differences to generator capability, intent preservation to original-prompt conditioning and episodic rewards, and training stability to initialization, LoRA and a fixed environment. It also explains early denoised-state usefulness and argues that relative policy overhead decreases with larger generators.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses approximately three days per training run, the GPT-5 model snapshot, DanceGRPO training and code information, and the models used for semantic-recall evaluation. Existing GRPO, LoRA, hardware, resizing and prompting details remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The named prompt datasets and alignment tasks remain Pick-a-Pic v2, RePrompt prompts and GenEval; the new generator configurations do not establish new data coverage. However, v2 Appendix C.4 introduces DanceGRPO training on its unspecified 'official' dataset, so the PDFs cannot establish whether this adds different represented data.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-5 to the single- and composite-reward comparisons and DanceGRPO to the SD1.5 composability experiment (Tables 1–2). DanceGRPO was only discussed as prior work in v1. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols are retained, but substantial new evaluation settings are introduced: inference timing on one A100 with batch size 8, BERTScore and LLM-based intent recall, FLUX.1-dev and SD3.5-large configurations, and a Qwen3-VL-4B policy ablation. DanceGRPO additionally uses 50 training epochs with HPSv2 reward.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and refinement-step ablations, v2 tests prompt-length growth, semantic drift, interpretability of early denoised feedback, training stability and stronger policy initialization (Appendices D.2–D.3 and E.2–E.3). Runtime profiling also directly examines the cost of additional refinement steps.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 11 explicitly reports average token counts with standard-deviation bands. v1 already contains shaded bands in Figure 6, which are retained, but lacks this explicitly identified variability statistic. No additional repeated-run counts, seeds or significance tests are specified.

E6.justification: All original score rows in v1 Tables 2–4 are retained in v2 Tables 1–3. Added results include GPT-5 and DanceGRPO comparisons, flow-matching transfer scores, runtime measurements and new diagnostic curves. Table 7 reports ImageReward 0.6922 with Qwen3-VL-4B versus 0.6320 with Qwen2.5-VL-3B, explicitly comparing different policy configurations.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix E.1 introduces an inference adaptation that converts flow-matching timesteps into diffusion timesteps with equivalent SNR before supplying them to the policy. The core MDP, GRPO training, sparse refinement and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are preserved. Changes include adding PromptLoop to the title, terminology and grammar corrections, an acknowledgment, and reorganizing the former additional-results appendix into prompt-evolution and additional-results sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint layout to two columns. The original MDP comparison table is incorporated into Figure 3, Figure 2 gains a preference/runtime panel, and GPT-5 columns expand comparison grids. New runtime, transfer and initialization tables and Figures 11–14 substantially expand the visual presentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Idea2Img to related work and references supporting denoised-state evaluation, flow-matching backbones and semantic scoring, including Free2Guide and BERTScore. Its central positioning relative to weight-level alignment and existing prompt-refinement approaches is retained.

T1.justification: The substantive diffusion equations, MDP definitions, GRPO objective and denoised-estimate formulation are retained. Correcting the sampled-action index in prose makes it consistent with the existing definition; no substantive theorem, proof or derivation is added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support for practicality and reliability: v1 lacks direct runtime and semantic-drift measurements, while v2 adds these alongside training diagnostics and transfer to flow-matching models. These address important validation gaps while retaining the original results. The 'negligible overhead' wording is overstated relative to Table 4's approximately 23% increase at five refinements, but the overall gain in evidence is substantial.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PromptLoop, with matching core methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original baseline comparisons, runtime measurements, transfer experiments and prompt-behavior analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-alignment experiments, component ablations and qualitative analyses in Tables 2–4, Figure 6 and Appendix D.

Its explicit claim to be the first framework automatically generating interactive web tasks is removed.

C2.justification: New Appendix D identifies dependence on accurate, complete KGs and restricted coverage beyond predefined relationships. Section 4.3 attributes KG-free multi-page failures to missing inter-page relations. The web-agent performance gap is newly interpreted as showing that the benchmark emphasizes multi-step reasoning rather than simple visual grounding.

The template difficulty list omits Expert, and single-agent error handling is relabeled partially supported. Conversely, v1's numerical coverage proportions disappear. Generation model, temperature, embeddings, evaluation prompts and project access information remain unchanged.

The ablation uses the same source coverage; OSWorld and MMBench receive descriptive comparisons, not reported evaluations on additional datasets.

Table 3 also adds UI-TARS-1.5-7B under both web-agent configurations. Tables 5–6 compare OSWorld, MMBench and TaskCraft descriptively rather than reporting numerical baseline runs.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces 1,000 generated tasks per method, divided equally between document and web tasks, with GPT-4o generation and two human annotators assessing consistency and solvability. v3 also adds a 100-node-pair graph check and a 50-trajectory evaluator audit. The ablation's agent configuration is ambiguous: its prose names Gemini 2.5 Flash, whereas Table 4 lists Qwen models.

E4.justification: v3 adds a central ablation testing whether KG structure improves generated-task quality, plus graph-edge verification and human validation of web-task judgments. Conversely, v1's document task-type performance analyses in Figures 6–7 disappear. The execution case study and exploratory safety-generation discussion are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for performance. The new graph-precision and human–judge agreement percentages are point-estimate validation results, not uncertainty estimates for the reported scores.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports document/web consistency of 0.95/0.78 versus 0.74/0.62 without KG, and solvability of 0.93/0.72 versus 0.73/0.60. v3 also reports 88% graph-edge precision, 88% human–judge agreement, and UI-TARS overall success rates of 0.0491 and 0.0719. Existing Table 2 and retained Table 3 scores are unchanged, while document task-type results are removed.

M1.justification: KG construction, Algorithm 1's sampling rules, template and meta-path task generation, MMR selection and agent architectures remain substantively unchanged. Appendix A newly documents filtering and content constraints without establishing that the underlying procedure was changed.

Existing experimental discussions are consolidated into Main Results, appendices are reordered, and duplicate task-template sections are merged. P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. v1's overview diagram, coverage chart and document performance plots are removed; v3 adds Tables 4–6 and expands Figure 1 and Table 3 for UI-TARS. R1.justification: v3 substantially revises positioning around semantic consistency and executability, adds discussion of Learn-by-Interact, and contrasts Graph2Eval's graph-based generation with TaskCraft's task composition. These are modest communication gains; the empirical evidence, technical documentation, and stated limitations remain unchanged.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark experiments, ablations, supplementary analyses, and qualitative results.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking RL's advantage over SFT to exploration and group-relative learning, attributing attribute transfer to broader learned distinctiveness, and attributing compositional preservation to HPSv3. It also interprets higher-count performance as generalization beyond memorization and explicitly excludes personalization from DISCO's scope. These extend the interpretations substantially, although some causal explanations lack isolating ablations.

The original training data, DiverseHumans, and MultiHuman-TestBench coverage remain.

E2.justification: Appendix E.1.4 adds a focused online supervised fine-tuning comparator, evaluated against DISCO in Table E.4. The original proprietary and open-source generator comparison sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include highest-reward-sample online SFT under the same prompts and curriculum, additional curriculum bounds, a blinded study with 25 participants judging 22 image pairs, and 270 samples spanning 2–10 people. Appendix F also introduces clothing-similarity and Qwen3-VL body-type scoring and GenEval2 evaluation. The original Appendix D settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses testing RL versus additional supervised training, curriculum-bound sensitivity, agreement with human judgments, extrapolation beyond trained person counts, transfer to other visual attributes, and per-person compositional control. The earlier reward-weight, aggregation-function, computational, and artifact analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1.8 newly reports correlation analysis between automated metrics and human judgments, although the correlation coefficient type and its uncertainty are unspecified. Existing shared image-index seeds and Figure 5's 95% confidence intervals remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: Original main-table and retained appendix scores are unchanged. New results include SFT versus DISCO UFA of 73.0 versus 98.6 (Table E.4), curriculum-bound outcomes, clothing similarity of 0.73/0.65/0.60 for Flux/face-DISCO/clothing-DISCO (Table F.1), and GenEval2 means of 24.6 versus 27.6 for Flux and DISCO (Table F.2). Human-study correlations and larger-crowd results further expand the findings.

M1.justification: The original Flow-GRPO procedure, four-component facial-diversity reward, curriculum, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. Appendix F.2 adds DISCO(Cloth), an adaptation replacing the ArcFace identity reward with Fashion-SigLIP clothing similarity.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution narrative are revised, the mathematical preliminaries are substantially condensed, and the conclusion and limitations are rewritten. Appendix E is reorganized, a dedicated generalizability section is introduced, and ethics and reproducibility receive numbered appendix headings. These changes substantially reshape the narrative despite extensive retained technical text.

P2.justification: v3 adds four tables covering SFT, curriculum bounds, attribute diversity, and GenEval2, plus four figures showing human judgments, larger-crowd performance, clothing diversity, and compositional examples. Original figure artwork is retained and relocated where needed; Figure 1 is resized and Table 2 gains a highlighted final row.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for CLIP, Qwen3-VL, GenEval2, concurrent diverse-video policy optimization, and Ar2Can. It briefly positions DISCO relative to concurrent video-diversity work and as a foundation for Ar2Can, while retaining the earlier related-work framework.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 removes the explicit rectified-flow interpolation and target velocity, ODE–SDE drift relationship, and trajectory-policy factorization, replacing this formal background with a shorter description and reference to Flow-GRPO. The DISCO reward mathematics and optimization objective are retained; no new proof is introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation by addressing v2's missing SFT control, human assessment of identity metrics, curriculum-bound sensitivity, and tests of extrapolation and general compositional capability. These additions support method choice and applicability while preserving the original main results. Reporting remains imperfect: the human-study correlations are incompletely specified, and the retained statement that no human subjects were used conflicts with the new 25-participant study. These limitations qualify, but do not outweigh, the broader evidential gains.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DISCO and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained algorithms and experiments can be matched across the additions, relocations, and renumbering.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds supervised fine-tuning comparisons, a participant study, curriculum experiments, and generalization evaluations.

before.justification: v2 reports original DISCO evaluations on DiverseHumans and MultiHuman-TestBench, component ablations, reward-weight experiments, and qualitative results.

The LVLM discussion replaces the argument about retrieval augmentation drawn from standalone-model comparisons with a hypothesis about landmark memorization. M1.justification: The architecture, semantic fusion and InfoNCE objective remain unchanged. However, v1 Section III.D describes multiplying cosine similarities, while v2 Section 3.4 explicitly applies softmax before multiplying probabilities. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes inference or documents a previously omitted step.

This exceeds isolated wording or numbering edits.

E2.justification: The new WindowsAgentArena comparison includes OpenCUA-7B and UltraCUA-7B, neither evaluated in v1. Existing OSWorld comparator membership is retained. UI-TARS-1.5-7B is not a newly introduced model: v1 already identifies that version in its experimental setup.

E3.justification: The reported IDM corpus changes from roughly 500K synthetic plus 132K Mind2Web transitions to approximately 600K synthetic transitions. The Mind2Web labeling test is replaced by a balanced holdout containing 100 transitions for each of six action types. WindowsAgentArena introduces a 15-step evaluation protocol; OSWorld retains its 50-step limit.

E4.justification: Tables 10–27 add detailed GIMP labeling, OSWorld VLC, and Windows File Explorer trajectory case studies. Appendix D.1 also briefly reports a qualitative NaFlex-versus-fixed-resolution comparison. The existing action/reasoning, retrieval, data-scaling, and application-domain analyses remain substantially unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's specified labeling-test sample size changes evaluation design, not uncertainty reporting; its discussion of predictive probabilities does not add a statistical evaluation.

E6.justification: New WindowsAgentArena results report 24.0% for W&L fine-tuning versus 18.1% without fine-tuning, 12.9% with TongUI labels, 13.5% for OpenCUA-7B, and 21.7% for UltraCUA-7B. Table 4 replaces labeling results and adds Release: W&L action accuracy is 91.6% on v1's Mind2Web test and 91.7% on v2's different holdout, not a comparable performance gain. Existing OSWorld results and retained appendix numerical analyses are unchanged.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 expands the action vocabulary from five primitives to six by adding Release and defining Click as a press event, enabling compositional drag-and-drop previously described as unsupported. Coordinate bins change from 0–1000 to 0–999. The core IDM, retrieval, and ICL/SFT pipeline remains intact; most appendix architecture additions are newly disclosed details.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and data-synthesis related work undergo extensive rewriting. v2 merges the separate ICL/SFT method subsections, reorganizes experimental setup and analysis, and restructures the appendices with dedicated architecture and training sections. The earlier LLM-use disclosure appendix is removed.

P2.justification: v2 redraws and crops Figure 2, adds the Windows results table, expands the labeling table with Release, and introduces extensive screenshot-and-action tables plus ICL prompt boxes. Table captions move above tables, and several displays are relocated or reordered. Figures 1 and 3 retain their underlying graphics.

R1.justification: v2 adds an OpenCUA/AgentNet annotation-cost comparison and references WindowsAgentArena, UltraCUA, Agent S/S2, agent-scaling work, and SigLIP-2. These update context and competitive positioning while preserving the main distinction between dedicated inverse-dynamics labeling and prior MLLM-based synthesis.

T1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies mathematical mappings for the previously underspecified action and coordinate heads and visual cross-attention in Equations 1–4. Appendix E largely formalizes the existing cross-entropy training description. This is a limited addition of mathematical definitions, without new theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: The Windows evaluation and substantially expanded collection, model, and prompt documentation improve empirical breadth and reproducibility beyond v1. The benefit is tempered by replacing the independent Mind2Web labeling test with a same-pipeline holdout and by inconsistencies in the new documentation, including frozen versus end-to-end encoder training and incompatible image/patch dimensions. These limits prevent the revision from establishing a substantial overall quality improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Watch & Learn with the same authors, core framework, and substantial shared experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains original OSWorld experiments and adds WindowsAgentArena results, a revised IDM labeling evaluation, and additional trajectory examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original IDM labeling evaluations, OSWorld ICL and fine-tuning results, ablations, and appendix data-scaling and application-level analyses.

before.justification: v2 reports original OSWorld-Verified and WindowsAgentArena evaluations, action-labeling measurements, ablations, and appendix analyses of data scaling and application domains.

These are substantive evaluation-design additions and configuration changes.

Conversely, it omits the additional appendix interpolation/transfer visualizations and LIBERO-10 action-replay analysis. The token-dimension ablation is retained unchanged as Table 8, and the existing data-scaling analysis is reorganized rather than newly introduced.

P2.justification: The document switches from a single-column preprint layout to two columns, substantially resizing and rearranging figures and tables. v2 expands comparison-table structures, adds transfer/planning/decoder-ablation tables, relocates the dimensionality table from the appendix, and omits appendix Figures 7–9. Retained probing and scaling plots are redisplayed rather than new results.

R1.justification: The related-work organization and principal positioning remain largely intact. v2 adds citations for comparison methods, datasets and additional VLA research. It removes MovieDreamer and the explicit acknowledgment in the introduction and method section that Zhao et al. inspired the diffusion-autoencoder approach.

T1.justification: The flow-matching objective, state-difference formulation, combined policy loss and probing equations are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation.

improvement.justification: The new quantitative transfer/planning tests, broader comparisons and decoder ablation strengthen evidence for generalization and design choices. However, v2 loses substantial training, probing and robot-protocol documentation and the concrete grasping-failure discussion, while referring to an unavailable appendix. Its newly described encoder replacement also complicates interpreting revised benchmark results. These empirical gains and reproducibility losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same StaMo work, with matching methods, equations and retained results. v1 includes Appendices A–C; supplied v2 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix. This observable omission can be assessed alongside the retained and added material.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative ManiSkill transfer and planning evaluations, expanded comparisons and a decoder-pretraining ablation.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, LIBERO policy evaluation, co-training, action-probing and real-robot results, plus appendix ablations and action-replay experiments.

C1.justification: The central reasoning claim is substantively narrowed. v1 presents structured traces as faithful, verifiable reasoning; v2 emphasizes transparent intermediate behavior and modality-aware soft scaffolds, explicitly disclaiming guaranteed faithfulness. The single-model, retrieval-free contribution and reported accuracy advantage remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly allows redundant or spurious path hops, additional composer cues, and answer-oriented selection that may produce unintuitive or unfaithful explanations. Its conclusion acknowledges path–explanation mismatches beyond v1's existing hallucination caveat. It also adds an interpretation of the revised timings as supporting practical deployment.

D1.justification: Most training settings move from v1 Appendix A.1.1 into v2 Section 5.1. However, v2 removes all three exact prompt templates, path-serialization instructions, and details such as the selector's ground-truth input and Gemini Dynamic Thinking mode. It adds coverage-filtering instructions and vLLM/L20-server information, leaving substantially different reproducibility documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on OK-VQA and FVQA and test transfer in both directions. Revised qualitative examples remain within this coverage; no additional dataset, domain, or distinct evaluation scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds the Qwen2.5-VL-7B CoT + SFT comparator to Tables 1 and 2. In the retained ship and sofa case studies, it removes Qwen and Llama baseline responses while retaining Gemma-3-12B and Gemini 2.5 Pro. Other quantitative comparator sets remain unchanged.

Its vLLM timing context is newly disclosed information, without an established before-and-after protocol change.

E4.justification: Component ablations, K sensitivity, and cross-domain analyses remain. Qualitative analysis contracts from five examples in v1 Tables 5–9 to revised ship and sofa examples in v2 Tables 5–6, removing the venue, wind-strength, and Canadian-location cases and reducing backbone-specific evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 42 and single-run reporting. Neither reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v2 condenses the existing disclosure rather than introducing a different statistical practice.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy entries in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged, while CoT + SFT adds 79.58% on OK-VQA and 75.13% on FVQA. Figure 3 substantially revises construction times from approximately 9–44 seconds to 0.5–2.2 seconds per example. Several qualitative outputs are removed or replaced with different traces. The timing revision is not an established same-setting speedup because comparable execution conditions are not documented.

M1.justification: The planner, composer, same-model selector, training objective, and single-pass inference remain. However, v2 Section 4.2 explicitly rejects low-coverage explanations before selection, whereas v1 describes path binding and theoretical coverage constraints without this operational step. The PDFs do not establish whether filtering is newly introduced or newly documented.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and conclusion, changes the title, removes the research-question organization, and condenses baseline, implementation, and metric material into Section 5.1. The appendix structure is removed, with selected content incorporated into the main text.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column presentation. Figure 2's example paths and caption are revised, Figure 3's time axes change, ablation rows receive descriptive names, and cross-domain deltas gain color coding. Three prompt figures and three case-study tables disappear; the two retained cases are condensed and relocated.

R1.justification: The related-work coverage is largely retained. Mikolov et al. (2013) disappears with the discussion rejecting Word2Vec-based scoring. Positioning more explicitly contrasts modality-aware structured scaffolds with generic chain-of-thought supervision, without a substantial expansion of cited research.

T1.justification: v2 removes all of v1 Appendix A.3: trace-feasibility definitions, the Rademacher-complexity claim, selector MLE/MAP analysis, KL-based self-distillation results, and the likelihood-bound derivation and proofs. The main task and method equations remain.

improvement.justification: The added CoT + SFT control and explicit faithfulness limitations improve comparison and claim calibration. However, removing exact prompts and serialization details weakens reproducibility, while the substantially revised timings and replacement case-study traces lack enough provenance to assess their evidential quality. With main accuracy results unchanged, these benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StaR-KVQA, with matching core components, datasets, and main experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable, including v1's appendix and image-based prompts. The supplied v2 ends with references and contains no appendix.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion distinguishing VOLD from Thinking Machines Lab's text-only on-policy distillation, plus references supporting GSPO, the new benchmarks and the perception–reasoning trade-off. The central positioning relative to KDRL and X-Reasoner remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the policy definitions and alignment rationale are retained. The GSPO extension is described verbally without adding a formal derivation, theorem or proof.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–7 and Figure 6 improve empirical support by exposing perception losses, testing image-based RL initialization and substantiating the previously asserted compatibility with other RL algorithms. The gains are limited by sparse training details for the new experiments and an attribution of perception loss to reasoning training that the comparisons do not causally isolate. The core method and original results remain unchanged.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VOLD research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds multimodal capability evaluation, image-based RL experiments and GSPO learning curves in its supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original VOLD benchmark evaluations, component ablations, learning curves and appendix experiments on teacher size, alignment duration and KL masking.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain context preservation during fine-tuning and context marginalization during generation to improve synthetic training data. The abstract and introduction retain the headline Aircraft comparison and superiority in 18 of 24 settings. Added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that prompt diversity matters but does not fully explain BOB's advantage. Its new limitations paragraph makes reliable class-agnostic attributes an explicit applicability condition and identifies automatic attribute discovery and coarse-grained ImageNet recognition as challenges. These refine the existing mechanism and scope rather than replace them.

D1.justification: The existing hyperparameter and generation tables and validation-set instructions are retained. v2 documents settings for its new sweeps, including epoch adjustments, but removes v1's explicit code-availability statement and repository link. This is a change in access documentation; the PDFs do not establish that the code itself became unavailable.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Aircraft, Car, CUB, and Pets for few-shot classification and CUB-LT and Flower-LT for long-tail classification. The new sample-count sweeps and qualitative examples use retained datasets and tasks; ImageNet is not added as a downstream evaluation benchmark.

E2.justification: The seven main comparison methods remain unchanged. v2 Table 3 adds explicit prompt-source comparison variants using Diff-II's dataset-level suffixes and 100 GPT-generated background/pose descriptions. These are evaluated alternatives to BOB's extracted contexts, rather than newly added full benchmark baselines.

E3.justification: The main splits, backbones, generation settings, and training protocols are retained. New Aircraft experiments vary real images per class over 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16, and synthetic images over 100–500. The synthetic-data sweep reduces classifier epochs to 100, 50, 33, 25, and 20 to approximately hold gradient updates constant.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis with prompt-diversity controls, real- and synthetic-data scaling, joint versus independent context sampling, attribute composition, seed stability, and qualitative comparisons on Car, CUB, and Pets. Existing epoch, FID, and caption-model analyses remain. The class-level ablation with preservation moves into Table 3; its counterpart without preservation is omitted.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 Section 7.5 explicitly reports three additional runs of five-shot Aircraft using different few-shot images, with individual seed results for BOB and DataDream in Table 8. This adds localized repeatability evidence, but no confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty summaries for the main benchmark tables.

E6.justification: All original per-dataset scores in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for prompt sources, data scaling, attributes, and seeds. Examples include 72.10% for GPT-generated contexts versus 73.78% for BOB, and 61.09% with color versus 60.31% with background/pose. The 68.01% ablation entry disappears. Pets overlap reporting changes from 22/39 to 25/37 with revised mappings. New Table 1 averages include an error: MAE/Diff-II five-shot is printed as 72.69%, although its listed scores average 72.96%.

M1.justification: The main two-stage BOB pipeline, architectures, and objectives remain unchanged. Section 7.4 adds evaluated procedural variants that sample background and pose independently or incorporate color as another attribute. These are limited adaptations tested through ablations, not replacements for the default method.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose are retained. v2 rewrites the context-marginalization explanation, expands the five-shot versus ten-shot discussion, edits wording and author information, and reorganizes Appendices A/B into supplementary Sections 6/7. These are localized narrative revisions alongside the new scientific material.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the main paper from one column to two, adds an opening comparison figure, and adds several supplementary plots and image grids. It combines the FID and caption-model plots, converts the epoch table into a plot, adds average columns to Table 1, and restructures the component-ablation display.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu et al.'s work on feasibility of synthetic training data and removes Pearl's Causality reference. Related-work positioning shifts emphasis from integrating diverse captions across stages toward preserving controllability and marginalizing spurious associations. The broader related-work coverage remains stable.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the causal graph and back-door adjustment formula but removes v1's explicit sample-ID definition, the independence argument P(I|Y) approximately equals P(I), and the written confounding path. This reduces the formal justification without adding a theorem or changing the retained adjustment identity.

improvement.justification: The new prompt controls, controlled data-quantity sweeps, attribute tests, and three additional seeds strengthen understanding and robustness evidence beyond v1's existing evaluations. Explicit applicability limitations also improve qualification of the claims. The gain is limited because most new quantitative analysis concerns Aircraft and the main benchmark results are unchanged. Removal of the code link and the erroneous new Table 1 average partly offset these benefits.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BOB research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial formatting changes.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds prompt-source comparisons, data-quantity sweeps, attribute ablations, and results from additional seeds.

before.justification: v1 reports original few-shot and long-tail classification experiments, component ablations, distribution comparisons, and training-duration analyses.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central representation-bottleneck claim remains. v3 narrows the novelty framing from a 'novel geometric regularization loss' to applying established temporal contrastive principles, explicitly emphasizes controlled diagnosis, and no longer lists state-of-the-art performance as a main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning environment complexity, visual artifacts, temporal-Transformer overhead and a still-large oracle gap. This qualifies v1's minimal-overhead discussion and more general residual-misalignment caveat. Conversely, explanations tied to the removed ablations, including projection/reconstruction decoupling and adjacent-only shortcuts, disappear.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1's training Table 4, including optimizer schedules, regularization weights, architecture settings and sampling parameters, and substitutes a repository link for the earlier promised release. It adds oracle implementation and image-normalization details. Minecraft documentation now specifies recorded state trajectories rendered with Blender, whereas v1 specified Malmo collection; this does not establish that the dataset or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Supplement C in v3 adds evaluated Atari environments Asterix and Breakout, extending coverage from static 3D navigation environments to dynamic game settings. The original two maze datasets and Minecraft environment remain. The Atari extension is explicitly limited to two games.

E2.justification: The main Standard Diffusion, Video Diffusion, Diffusion Forcing and oracle comparisons remain. However, the supplementary comparisons against Adjacent-Only regularization, no-projection and single-loss variants disappear with v1's detailed ablations. No new external comparison method is demonstrated.

E3.justification: v3 adds SSIM and rFID evaluation on Maze 9x9 and PSNR/SSIM evaluation for Atari. The retained frame-wise MSE comparisons, rollout horizons and held-out MLP probing procedure are unchanged. The added evaluations are sparsely specified; no change to retained training budgets or rerunning of existing experiments is established.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix B reports loss-term removal, projection-head removal, latent dimensions 16/32/64/128, and all-pairs versus adjacent-only regularization studies. Their tables, curves and detailed findings are absent from v3. Section 7 and Supplement E merely list these studies and refer to supplementary results. Latent probing, clustering and rollout case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both mention a fixed seed for maze-map generation, rather than seed-based uncertainty estimation. The added tables likewise report single estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 3's rollout curves and Table 1's probing scores are unchanged. v3 adds perceptual and Atari results: for example, its Table 2 reports DF rFID of 4.4345 for the baseline versus 2.8729 with regularization, and Table 3 reports Breakout PSNR of 34.23 versus 37.76. v1's detailed ablation results disappear. These are added and removed results, not same-setting improvements between versions.

M1.justification: The CNN plus causal Transformer encoder, instantaneous decoder, normalized projection head, all-pairs slowness loss, uniformity loss and combined reconstruction/KL objective are unchanged. The expanded oracle description documents the existing diagnostic experiment; the Atari results do not establish a method adaptation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related Work, Representation as the Bottleneck and Limitations become separate sections, the oracle explanation expands, and the appendices are reordered. This substantially changes the narrative despite retaining much of the method and experimental text.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to two columns, substantially resizing and relocating figures. v1's ablation plots/tables and training table disappear, while two new supplementary result tables appear. Retained trajectory/environment figures are relocated and renumbered; clustering panels lose their axes, with normalization explained in the caption.

R1.justification: v3 adds a substantial Related Work section and many references covering video-world-model architectures, latent representations and temporal contrastive learning. It explicitly positions GRWM as using established contrastive principles to regularize a world-model autoencoder, expanding and refining v1's shorter positioning around trajectory regularization.

T1.justification: The deterministic formulation and mathematical definitions of the representation and losses remain unchanged. Neither version develops formal guarantees or proofs. v3's additional oracle equations explain an existing implementation rather than introduce new theoretical reasoning.

improvement.justification: v3 improves positioning, oracle explanation and limitations, and adds perceptual metrics and limited dynamic-environment validation. However, it removes the detailed component ablations and in-PDF training configuration, weakening support for design choices and reproducibility while retaining references to missing ablation results. The linked repository's contents are not established by the PDFs. These material gains and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRWM research. All 17 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v3, including appendices, were readable. Retitling, reorganization and identifiable content omissions do not prevent reliable comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains original rollout and representation results and adds Maze 9x9 perceptual metrics and Atari experiments in supplementary Tables 2–3.

before.justification: v1 reports original rollout experiments, latent probing and clustering, and component ablations across three deterministic environments.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain MeasureBench, controllable synthesis, evidence of fine-grained perception failures, and preliminary synthetic-data training gains with limited real-world transfer. Although v2's abstract describes transfer more positively, its introduction and conclusion retain the qualification. The expanded experiments principally strengthen evidence for the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning SFT overfitting, limited benefits from procedural instructions, stronger RFT gains on simpler instruments, and mitigation of clock-time priors. The electricity-meter case changes from faulting left-to-right reading to accepting the procedure and attributing failure to pointer localization (v1 Appendix A.1 versus v2 D.1). It also removes v1's inference that similar model ordering establishes strong synthetic-to-real transferability.

D1.justification: v2 identifies FlagEvalMM for evaluation and verl for training, specifies GPT-5.2-generated SFT rationales, and discloses avoidance of real clock images showing 10:10 and uniform synthetic clock-time sampling. It also mentions code releases while retaining the project-page address. These disclosures do not establish changes to the existing dataset or implementation; the main GRPO hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluations on MMMU, MMMU-Pro, MathVista, and TextVQA to test retention of broader capabilities (Table 5), substantially extending task coverage beyond instrument reading. MeasureBench itself retains the same 2,442 examples and instrument coverage; the synthetic-type count of 17 in v1 Section 2.4 becomes 16, consistent with Table 1 in both versions.

E2.justification: v2 introduces answer-only and rationale-based SFT as substantive training comparators to GRPO (Table 6). It also adds Qwen3-VL-8B to the main and thinking comparisons and GPT-4.1-Mini to prompt experiments. The traditional systems were already evaluated in v1 Appendix A.7; v2 Table 7 retains them and adds Qwen3-VL-8B to that comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols compare general versus instrument-specific prompts, with and without a precision suffix, excluding 10.53% of prompts deemed immutable. v2 also tests detailed instructions, two SFT response formats, and GRPO on Qwen2.5-VL-3B. The existing GRPO training budget remains 3,900 synthetic examples and 15 epochs. These additions do not establish that retained experiments used changed settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds prompt-sensitivity and instructional-guidance analyses, SFT-versus-GRPO transfer comparisons, checks for degradation on general benchmarks, per-instrument training gains, and a before/after analysis of the clock-time bias. Integer-output diagnostics expand across model families, while v1's [0,1] distribution panels are removed. The soft-margin ablation is retained in the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The expanded numerical-output distributions describe model behavior rather than introducing uncertainty estimation for performance results.

E6.justification: New prompt, SFT, general-benchmark, and 3B-model results substantially expand the evidence. Retained scores also change: Gemini-2.5-Pro's real/synthetic overall accuracy becomes 30.2/26.3 instead of 30.3/26.1, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B becomes 14.6/10.9 instead of 15.5/11.0. Its GRPO real-world score changes from 20.1 to 19.7. Clock-bias and traditional-system results also change; the PDFs do not explain all revisions to retained scores.

M1.justification: The registry-based 2D/3D synthesis pipeline, GRPO procedure, correctness-plus-format reward, and soft-margin alternative remain substantively unchanged. Moving the soft-margin reward to Appendix A.2 and applying GRPO to another model size do not introduce a new proposed method.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial reorganization: the traditional-system comparison moves into Section 3.8, reward design and training results receive separate subsections, and the former Appendix A.1–A.7 is reorganized into Appendices A–F. The introduction and synthesis description are condensed and rewritten, and distribution analysis is redistributed between the main text and appendices.

P2.justification: v1 Tables 2 and 3 are merged into v2 Table 2, and the synthesis schematic and example figures are combined. v2 adds experimental tables and an instrument-gain bar chart, redraws distribution plots, reorders the category heatmap, and revises electricity-meter annotations. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering and numerical updates.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for FlagEvalMM and HybridFlow, plus formal citations for previously discussed benchmarks including MMBench, MM-Vet, SEED-Bench, MathVision, and MathVerse. The central positioning against fragmented, instrument-specific evaluations remains substantially unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 rewrites the existing reward using indicator notation and alpha = 0.9, while retaining the same interval-distance, margin, and partial-credit definitions. Relocating the soft-margin equations does not change their mathematics. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support by testing alternative explanations that v1 left largely unexamined: prompt wording, procedural guidance, and whether synthetic-data gains depend on GRPO rather than SFT (Tables 3, 4, and 6). General-benchmark checks and another trained model size further strengthen the training analysis. These gains outweigh localized reporting weaknesses: Table 7 repeats full-benchmark VLM scores despite describing a dial-meter subset, leaving comparison scope unclear, and Section 3.6 claims no degradation although Table 5 shows small MathVista and TextVQA declines.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeasureBench study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and revised content.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds prompt experiments, supervised fine-tuning comparisons, general-benchmark evaluations, and GRPO results for a 3B model.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 17 VLMs, thinking-mode comparisons, GRPO training experiments, numerical-output analyses, and tests of traditional gauge-reading systems.

C1.justification: The central claims remain identifying co-occurrence-induced prompt-pool confusion, addressing it through parameterized prompts and constrained fusion, and achieving superior VOC/COCO performance, particularly over longer task sequences. Consolidating four contribution bullets into three and shortening the conclusion do not change these claims' substantive scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix B.4 add explanations for why background information benefits P2IOD but interferes with prompt-pool matching. They also interpret compression results through representational capacity, convergence difficulties and limited forgetting in SAC's fully connected layer. These extend the existing mechanism discussion without replacing its central account.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link in the abstract and documents the new SAC module's pooling operations and layer dimensions. The existing optimizer, learning rates, training schedules, hardware and batch-size descriptions are unchanged. Conversely, the cross-task prompt comparison no longer explicitly identifies its former 5+5+5+5 setting.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VOC2007 and MS COCO detection coverage and COCO/Objects365 pretraining sources. The new compression study uses existing VOC coverage. COCO 40+40 and 70+10 experiments were already present in v1's supplementary Table 5.

E2.justification: Faster ILOD is added to the VOC single-step comparison in Table 1, although it already appeared in Table 4. LEA is added to COCO comparisons in Tables 2 and 5. New Table 9 also compares additional MD-DETR compression variants.

E3.justification: Table 6 replaces a VOC 10+10 fusion-threshold experiment with a reported 5+5+5+5 experiment and changes the tested threshold combinations. Appendix B.4 adds compression controls. The main metrics, dataset splits and training-budget descriptions remain unchanged. However, B.2 still describes the former 10+10 experiment, leaving the executed protocol ambiguous.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.4 and Table 9 substantially expand the analysis of proposal compression, testing SAC, removal of its fully connected layer, averaging and no compression across P2IOD and MD-DETR. The fusion-threshold evidence is replaced, while the original Figure 1 similarity-weight heatmap is removed. Existing component, hidden-dimension, sparsity and cross-task prompt analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both implementation appendices state that reported accuracy averages three independent trials. Neither version adds seed specifications, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 9 reports distinct compression outcomes: MD-DETR reaches 64.0 AP50 with SAC versus 61.5 with QL, while P2IOD reaches 64.7 with SAC versus 76.4 with averaging. Existing scores also change: Table 1's Objects365 P2IOD 19+1 overall AP50 rises from 88.8 to 89.1, and Table 4's Objects365 MD-DETR 5+5+5+5 overall score changes from 80.1 to 75.8. Table 6 supplies replacement results under a differently labeled setting, not a comparable performance gain.

M1.justification: Appendix B.4 introduces and evaluates an auxiliary Self-Attention Compression module using average/max pooling, a shared fully connected layer and sigmoid attention, including a variant without the fully connected layer. The main P2IOD method retains its MLP prompts, fusion and sparse loss. Averaging all proposals was already specified in v1; the expanded background-proposal discussion does not establish a new main-method input.

P1.justification: The title is shortened, the introduction and conclusion are streamlined, and the contribution list is consolidated. Pseudo-labeling moves from Methods Section 4.4 to Preliminaries Section 3.2, and supplementary sections receive lettered labels. Most of the method and experimental narrative retains its previous organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from an empirical similarity heatmap to a comparative method schematic. Figures 4-5 are redrawn with revised markers, legends and axis styling. Comparison tables gain rows, Table 6 is restructured, and Table 9 is added; the principal framework and qualitative detection displays remain.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly attributes task-vector decomposition to TIES-Merging and describes pseudo-labeling as the same method used by MD-DETR, rather than proposing a heuristic. It expands citations, including LEA and additional continual-learning/distillation work, and removes Aljundi et al. (2019). The overall positioning around prompt-pool limitations in IOD remains stable.

T1.justification: Equations (6)-(7) move prompt concatenation outside the key/value projection matrices, a non-equivalent mathematical revision. Appendix B.4 adds the SAC attention definition in Equation (10) and a parameter-size comparison. The fusion rule remains equivalent, and neither version provides theoretical proofs.

improvement.justification: The added compression study, baseline comparisons, clearer attribution and code-access information improve the paper's evidential coverage and documentation. However, v3's revised Table 6 conflicts with B.2 about the task setting, best thresholds and benefits of averaging: the text retains the old 10+10 and 0.7/0.3 conclusions while the table reports 5+5+5+5 and favors 0.3/0.3. The original diagnostic heatmap is also removed. These useful additions and substantive reporting regressions leave the net quality direction uncertain.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same P2IOD research, despite the shortened title in v3. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete supplementary materials are readable and support comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains original detection experiments and adds proposal-compression experiments in Appendix B.4 and Table 9.

before.justification: v1 reports original PASCAL VOC2007 and MS COCO experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and qualitative detection results, including supplementary experiments.

C1.justification: The central dataset, mask-aware model and improved findings-generation claims remain. V2 adds an explicit novelty claim in the abstract that its five-physician evaluation is the first human study of automated PET reporting.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges hallucinated numerical measurements and qualifies the reader evaluation by explaining their exclusion. It also discusses PET domain shift, possible overrating by automated metrics and external generalization. Dependence on supplied masks and a future fully automated reporting pipeline were already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: V2's supplement supplies acquisition and deidentification details, the formatting prompt, software libraries, LoRA placement, precision, batch size, learning rate and other hyperparameters. It also documents reader blinding, numerical masking, viewing software and scoring rubrics. These are substantial new disclosures, although conflicting epoch counts and training descriptions limit reproducibility.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on 32 external autoPET instances, extending coverage beyond the internal PET/CT dataset. The supplement identifies an additional imaging difference: primarily contrast-enhanced CT externally versus primarily non-contrast CT internally. Renaming PETAR-11K to PETARSeg-11K does not itself change coverage.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Table 3, v2 Table 2 adds QoQ-Med and fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B and MedGemma-4B comparisons. The added fine-tuned 2D baselines materially strengthen comparisons under dataset adaptation. Expanded names for retained baselines are not counted as new methods.

E3.justification: The reported internal test size changes from 1,170 to 1,175, and the stated anatomical pretraining size changes from approximately 5,000 to 100,000 segmentations. V2 reports ten epochs for all stages instead of five for initial pretraining, although supplementary Table 9 still lists five. It also specifies three-view inputs for the new fine-tuned 2D comparisons and changes retained ablation rows' TS flags from enabled to disabled. These are reported setting revisions, not evidence that all experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds an explicit full-model comparison with and without TotalSegmentator pretraining, which v1's populated ablation rows did not isolate. It also adds external distribution-shift evaluation, replaces the original qualitative cases with broader baseline error comparisons in Figure 4, and supplies autoPET examples in supplementary Figure 5.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates, whereas v2 Table 5 adds plus/minus quantities to physician ratings. Their statistical meaning is not specified. Neither version reports training-run uncertainty, seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: PETAR's reported BLEU, CIDEr and GREEN change from 0.531, 0.415 and 0.246 to 0.535, 0.457 and 0.257; changed settings prevent interpreting these as controlled performance gains. GREEN's human correlation changes from 0.608 to 0.592, and other metric correlations and rankings change. V2 additionally reports new comparator results, internal physician scores and preference counts (15 preferred, 54 tied, 47 not preferred), external ratings and cohort statistics.

M1.justification: The core encoding, focal cropping, feature fusion and autoregressive objective remain unchanged. Section 4.4 changes the stated alignment order from mask-then-projector to projector-then-mask and describes repeating the three-stage sequence on both training datasets. However, v2's stage headings contradict their descriptions, leaving the implemented order uncertain.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, results and explanatory passages. It reorganizes experimental setup and human evaluation, replaces the standalone PETAR-Bench and Discussion sections with revised setup and limitations sections, renames the dataset, and adds a structured supplement.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are substantially redrawn, and Figure 4 becomes a larger comparison matrix with anatomical error annotations. V2 removes the model-capability table, redesigns the dataset comparison table, reorganizes experimental tables and adds physician-results and supplementary displays. These changes extend well beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands citations supporting baseline models, PET datasets, evaluation metrics, implementation tools and segmentation workflows. It sharpens the distinction from Reg2RG's organ-level, single-modality setting and develops the relationship to Describe Anything's focal prompting; Describe Anything was already cited in v1.

T1.justification: The cropping, encoding, fusion and likelihood equations retain their mathematical substance. V2 makes mask embeddings and notation more explicit and numbers more equations, but introduces no substantive theoretical result, proof or changed formal assumption.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves a major evidential gap by publishing quantitative physician outcomes that v1's clinical-utility claims lacked, adding a limited external evaluation and testing fine-tuned 2D competitors. Its supplement materially improves methodological transparency, including disclosure that numerical hallucinations were excluded from reader scoring. Conflicting training-stage descriptions, epoch counts and some prose/table values remain, but the strengthened clinical evidence and documentation provide a substantial net improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PETAR-4B and the same core dataset of 11,356 lesions from 5,126 exams. Their text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. V2 includes supplementary material absent from the supplied v1, despite v1 referring to supplementary details.

after.justification: V2 reports original model comparisons, ablations, metric correlations and physician evaluations on internal and external data in Tables 2–5, with additional analyses in its supplement.

before.justification: V1 reports original model comparisons, component ablations and correlations between automated metrics and physician scores in Tables 3–5.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: V2's abstract and introduction explicitly claim improved video visual fidelity alongside motion and image diversity, extending v1's emphasis on diversity and preservation of key capabilities. The central data-free framework, theoretical contribution and SOTA/largest-distillation claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 questions the additional VBench rankings using claimed human preferences and interprets proximity to teacher scores as distribution preservation. It attributes four-phase gains to both SGTS removal and additional parameters, acknowledges greater complexity, and recommends matching phases to teacher experts. Existing mechanism explanations and Qwen-Image diversity limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents 64-GPU training, FSDP, checkpointing, context parallelism, Euler sampling, timestep schedules and shifts, resolution-sampling probabilities, noise clamps and phase-specific trainable components. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's optimizer and resolution settings. The promised code/model release becomes a stated availability link, whose contents were not externally checked.

E1.justification: Both retain the four-value toy distribution, text-to-image evaluation with 21 prompts, and video evaluation with 220 text prompts and 220 image-prompt pairs. Added metrics and expert configurations do not introduce new datasets, tasks or domains.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the base models, vanilla few-step DMD and the SGTS-based baseline. V2 renames v1's 'DMD with SGTS' to 'DMD2'; matching descriptions and retained scores establish continuity. The four-phase variant is an ablation of the proposed method.

E3.justification: V2 adds FID/FVD against base-model outputs and five additional VBench metrics, plus four-phase and partial-expert evaluations. Table 1 changes the reported I2V teacher from Wan2.2-T2V-A14B to Wan2.2-I2V-A14B. The toy network description changes from four MLPs to a four-layer MLP; these reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a quantitative four-step/two-phase versus four-step/four-phase comparison testing complete SGTS removal with additional experts (Table 6). Figure 12 compares the low-SNR expert's two-step output with the complete four-step pipeline to examine expert roles. Existing noise-interval, fixed-noise and high-SNR-training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both specify seeds 0–7 for image diversity and seed 42 for video evaluation, without repeated-training statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests. Parenthesized percentages in v2 Tables 4–5 are differences from base-model scores, not uncertainty estimates.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redrawn, comparison figures gain methods and examples, and the ablation display is redesigned. Reconstruction tables are reorganized by dataset, with NeRSemble moved to the supplement. Numerous new loss-analysis, robustness, editing, and computational-cost displays materially expand the visual presentation.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion and citations for SphereHead, FaceLift, Avat3r, inversion/diffusion approaches, and perceptual representations, while dropping the GRM and Feng et al. (2021) references. The existing positioning relative to GAN/NeRF pipelines and conventional supervision remains broadly intact.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly defines tanh-bounded FLAME-relative Gaussian positions in Equation 3 and a multiplicative perceptual-loss combination in Equation 7, details left unspecified in v1. These are limited mathematical additions; the decoder recurrence is retained, and no theorems or proofs are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens experimental support and reproducibility through relevant new comparators, a separately trained LPIPS+L1 control, targeted loss diagnostics, robustness tests, and detailed training specifications. Its more explicit temporal and editing limitations also improve claim calibration. These gains address important weaknesses in v1 and outweigh local reporting problems, including Table 5's SSIM heading above values around 15–16.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PercHead, with matching authors, core architecture, reconstruction tasks, and editing framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction and editing experiments, revised quantitative results, and additional loss diagnostics, robustness tests, and lightweight-model evaluations.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results on Ava-256 and NeRSemble, quantitative ablations, video reconstructions, and image- and text-conditioned editing examples.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly frames the abstract around human-centric generation and promotes the already-reported benefit of staged multi-task training into the abstract and introduction. The conclusion drops the explicit claim that FAM adds no significant computational overhead. The principal architectural contributions and overall performance claims remain.

C2.justification: The supplement adds explanations for interleaved and before-self-attention module placement, and identifies an alignment-versus-image-quality tradeoff for unrestricted MA-CFG. It explains restricted guidance as a mitigation. Section 11 newly states concrete limitations: absent video-aligned ambient-sound generation and constrained multi-person audio generation associated with the text encoder.

D1.justification: Sections 6–7 supply previously unavailable details: A2V window size 1/2, handling of one-frame versus four-frame video latents, 50-step Euler sampling, Vocos decoding, guidance scales 3 and 2, interval [0.5, 1], empty-text unconditional sampling, and the full Gemini scoring prompt. Section 10 additionally documents interaction insertion choices. These substantially expand reproducibility information without demonstrating changes to the retained experiments.

E1.justification: Supplement Section 9 adds public-benchmark evaluation on GRID for video-to-audio dubbing with unseen-speaker reference audio and EMTD for audio-driven half-body animation. These conditional tasks already appeared in v1's training framework, but their benchmark evaluation coverage is new. The original training datasets and 100-sample joint-generation test remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds StyleDubber and EmoDubber as evaluated dubbing comparators. Table 9 also explicitly compares MA-CFG against vanilla CFG and no CFG. The main Table 1 comparator set remains unchanged; the EMTD comparison and user study reuse existing baseline models.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 34-participant preference study assessing audio quality, video quality, and audiovisual coherence. New conditional evaluations use GRID Dubbing Setting 3.0 and EMTD, introducing LSE-D, FID, and FVD measurements alongside retained metrics. These are additional evaluation protocols; the original test composition, training budgets, and main evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplement Tables 7–8 newly test which layers receive interaction modules and where modules enter each DiT block. Table 9 quantitatively compares four guidance policies, including restricted-interval MA-CFG, extending v1's qualitative guidance analysis. The original interaction, FAM, and training-strategy ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three independent Gemini evaluations per sample. The supplement repeats this practice without introducing new seed counts, repeated-training information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. The 34-participant count describes the new study's sample size rather than an uncertainty-reporting change.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, apart from equivalent decimal formatting. New Table 4 reports UniAVGen preference shares of 68.90%, 62.60%, and 74.30% for AQ, VQ, and AVC. Table 5 reports GRID LSE-C/LSE-D/WER of 7.59/6.11/10.64, leading both dubbing comparators. EMTD results are mixed: UniAVGen has the best reported FID but worse FVD than both comparators. Tables 7–9 add placement and guidance results, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

M1.justification: The dual-branch architecture, asymmetric aligners, FAM, MA-CFG formulation, five task interfaces, and three-stage training remain unchanged. The supplement documents alignment, placement, and inference choices for the existing framework; it does not establish that the underlying method changed from v1.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. v2 revises the abstract, moves the introduction's task-unification discussion, clarifies the V2A motivation, shortens the conclusion, and adds acknowledgements. The new supplement has dedicated implementation, evaluation, ablation, and limitations sections, but the existing paper is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a compact three-task schematic to a full-width opening display with generated examples for four modes. Existing figures and tables are substantially resized, and Figure 5 is relocated. The supplement adds six tables, Tables 4–9, displaying new evidence rather than merely renumbering existing results.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for dubbing methods, benchmarks, inference components, and related generators, including VoiceCraft-Dub, MOVA, AudioX, and CMMD. However, the three-paradigm related-work organization and substantive positioning against UniVerse-1 and Ovi remain largely unchanged; this is an extension rather than a reframing.

T1.justification: The flow-matching losses, attention and interpolation equations, mask formulation, and guidance equations retain their mathematical substance. Changes to parameter-index notation are equivalent. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the supplementary implementation explanations do not introduce new theoretical results.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves support for the claimed task unification through GRID and EMTD evaluations and adds human preference evidence. The new placement and guidance ablations expose design choices and an important quality tradeoff, while implementation details and the evaluator prompt address major documentation gaps in the supplied v1. Explicit limitations also clarify applicability. Study-protocol detail and uncertainty reporting remain limited, but the added evidence and reproducibility information provide a substantial net improvement without relying on unchanged headline scores.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniAVGen, with matching authors, core methods, and main experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after the references; v2 additionally includes Supplementary Material, Sections 6–11, which was inspected.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a user study, conditional-generation benchmark results, and further ablations in supplementary Tables 4–9.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons in Table 1, interaction and modulation ablations in Tables 2–3, and qualitative and training-strategy results in Figures 4–7.

C2.justification: V1's brief calibration limitation becomes a broader discussion of coarse-grid limits for manipulation, restricted real-world coverage, the humanoid sim-to-real gap, and single-frame motion limitations. V2 also interprets calibration robustness versus clean accuracy, temporal fusion versus deployment cost, and semantic failures under rare weather/layout combinations.

D1.justification: Sections 9–11 newly document sensor synchronization, annotation and dynamic-object handling, voxel refinement, simulator capture, metadata, baseline adaptations, optimizers, schedules, normalization, and losses. Sections 6 and 8 add profiling and deployment details. These are substantial disclosures, although some grid-bound descriptions conflict. The repository destination and future-release wording remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same QuadOcc and H3O datasets and occupancy tasks. V2 extends test conditions through restricted-field-of-view inputs and controlled calibration perturbations. The KITTI tables document configuration adaptations; they do not establish an additional evaluated benchmark.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables is unchanged. Table 12 adds pose-aligned temporal averaging and BEVFormer-style temporal attention as comparative alternatives to single-frame OneOcc. Section 11 primarily documents existing baseline adaptations rather than establishing changes to those retained comparators.

E3.justification: V2 adds substantial experimental protocols: evaluation-only panorama cropping, expert and grid configurations, resolution scaling, deterministic calibration perturbations and noise-augmented retraining, three-frame fusion, and nested spatial evaluation ranges. It also introduces INT8/FP16 Jetson profiling. Newly disclosed settings for retained benchmarks do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's cumulative component ablation and lighting comparison, v2 adds expert-count/routing, field-of-view, Cartesian/cylindrical-grid, projection-path, resolution, calibration-noise, and temporal-fusion analyses. GDC visualizations, distance-wise comparisons, and a rainy-dusk semantic failure case further examine mechanisms and failure conditions.

E5.justification: V2 newly states that baseline seeds are fixed and calibration perturbations are deterministic by seed and frame ID. Jetson timings are explicitly averaged over 100 runs after five warm-ups. Neither version reports accuracy confidence intervals, error bars, or multi-seed variability; an increase in repeated training runs is not established.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 retain their scores, but v2 adds extensive results. Table 12 reports temporal-attention mIoU of 21.18/34.25 on QuadOcc/H3O-Heter, versus single-frame 20.56/32.23; Table 15 reports Jetson throughput of 13.64 FPS versus MonoScene's 10.20. Section 4.5 also changes allocated/reserved FP32 memory from 1.86/2.65 GB to 1.82/2.58 GB.

M1.justification: The core DP-ER, BGV, GDC, AMoE-3D architecture and loss remain unchanged. Section 6.7 adds evaluated three-frame extensions using pose-aligned feature averaging or BEVFormer-style temporal attention. The new explanation of bilinear lifting clarifies a procedure already specified in v1's equations.

P1.justification: The main text receives limited clarifications and editorial changes. The supplement substantially expands explanations of retained components, dataset construction, and baseline adaptations, using question/setup/findings/takeaway sections and consistent per-method templates. It also develops the previously brief limitations and outlook into an extensive discussion.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 5–19 and Tables 6–26, including projection illustrations, annotation pipelines, dataset statistics, runtime breakdowns, failure cases, and configuration tables. Some displays re-express existing information, such as semantic frequencies from Tables 2–3. Main Tables 2 and 4 are also compressed/reformatted while retaining their results.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting implementation and supplementary discussion, including Point-MoE/Point-MoDE, FAST-LIO2, CARLA, open-vocabulary occupancy, and occupancy world models/flow. These broaden supporting context while leaving the main related-work narrative and central research positioning largely unchanged.

T1.justification: The core model equations remain unchanged. V2 adds mathematical specifications for annotation voting and confidence, the empty-vote mask and gated refinement, and density-based label acceptance in Sections 9–10. Section 6.2 also defines AET as mIoU multiplied by FPS. These extend formal specification without adding theoretical guarantees or proofs.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation and transparency: measured Jetson runtime replaces v1's Thor extrapolation, targeted ablations test central design choices, and detailed benchmark-construction and baseline documentation address major reproducibility gaps. Failure analyses and explicit applicability limits also improve the balance of the claims. Conflicting voxel bounds in Sections 9–11 and Figure 7's inconsistent resolution caption still require clarification, but the added evidence and documentation provide a substantial net quality improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OneOcc, with matching core methods, datasets, and main experiments. The text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. V1 ends after its references; v2 adds supplementary Sections 6–13.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds experiments on projection choices, calibration robustness, temporal aggregation, resolution, field of view, and embedded-device runtime.

before.justification: V1 reports original QuadOcc and Human360Occ benchmark results, retrained baseline comparisons, component ablations, lighting analyses, and runtime measurements in Sections 4.1–4.5.
