E2.justification: Table 8 introduces comparisons with HULC, RoboFlamingo, and FLOWER on CALVIN; FLOWER is explicitly included as a reference result. The existing real-world comparisons with π0.5, VoxPoser, MOKA, and the supplementary PWTF-style variant are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated optimization cap from Kmax = 15 to 13, reducing optimization iterations from five to three while retaining ten initial proposals; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. New protocols include 40 CALVIN instruction chains with ground-truth segmentation, a five-value friction sweep, and up to three replanning attempts after execution failure.

The introduction and conclusion shift the Qwen-Image-2509 comparison from three-image performance to benchmark-level superiority, although the abstract retains its earlier three-image matching claim.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 removes the explicit conclusion that curated synthetic targets can substitute for real targets. Section 7.4.1 removes the interpretation linking very high facial similarity to copy-paste artifacts and its threshold rationale. Existing demographic limitations and appendix interpretations of style bias and evaluator coupling remain.

D1.justification: Section 7.1 changes a promised release upon acceptance to reported availability of the dataset, benchmark annotations and images, and complete evaluation scripts and prompts. v2 also documents face-source indices and a replaceable VLM interface. Conversely, it removes Table 2's ablation-column definitions and the per-type sampling allocations for the 75-case human study and 108-case style analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same source datasets, seven composition subtasks, 27 fine-grained types, De&Re task, and appendix application examples. The reduced benchmark sample counts do not establish changed task or population coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 newly reports Gemini-3-Pro-Image-Preview and GPT-Image-1.5 comparisons, including an overall score and task rankings, and adds a benchmark-level Qwen-Image-2509 comparison. However, Table 2 retains its original comparator rows, and Table 3 retains the same two methods; the expanded comparisons are documented only in prose.

E3.justification: MICo-Bench changes from 1,000 cases, grouped as 200/200/300/300, to 897 cases grouped as 138/168/291/300. Sections 4.2 and 7.4 replace GPT-4o scoring with GPT-5.4, Qwen2.5-VL-72B verification with Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct, and binary facial-preservation thresholds with graded scores. These substantially revise the reported evaluation protocol without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same De&Re ablation conditions remain in Table 2 despite removal of their explanatory prose. The appendix retains the human-alignment, style-homology, evaluator-coupling, copy-paste, demographic, and qualitative analyses. No new analytical question or robustness test is documented; revised numerical results are assessed under E6.

E5.justification: Both versions average human-ranking Spearman correlations across 25 participants and retain the same correlation-reporting procedures. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 extensively replaces scores: Qwen-Image's real-De&Re overall score changes from 58.2 to 35.9, BAGEL's from 44.3 to 34.4, and OmniGen2's from 51.2 to 33.8, reversing BAGEL and OmniGen2's ordering. These are results under revised conditions, not comparable performance declines. Section 5.2 additionally reports Gemini's 51.76 and new leadership findings absent from Table 2. Table 3 and appendix validation results remain unchanged.

M1.justification: The Compose-by-Retrieval and De&Re data-construction pipelines, generative architectures, and model fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged. Qwen-Image-MICo denotes the existing Qwen-MICo baseline. Evaluation-metric changes are assessed under E3 and T1.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the evaluator, benchmark, results, release, and metric-detail passages. v2 also adds Kai Cui and revises affiliations, corrects terminology and typos, and removes several explanatory paragraphs. The overall section structure and most main-text and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: All twenty figures and three tables are retained, with unchanged embedded example images and plots. Figure 6 moves between columns, appendix spacing changes, and several captions are revised. Table 2's new caption removes the ablation legend and describes different bolding semantics despite retaining the existing column structure.

R1.justification: v2 removes WithAnyone, cited as reference 90 in v1 to support the facial-similarity discussion. The remaining related-work discussion and research positioning are largely unchanged; subsequent reference renumbering is not a substantive change.

T1.justification: Section 7.4.1 substantively revises the visibility-weight definition: binary face acceptance above task-dependent thresholds becomes a five-level mapping to 0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.7, or 1, averaged with binary non-face scores. The geometric-mean SC/PQ definitions remain equivalent, and no theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves release documentation and specifies its revised evaluator, but weakens the connection between claims and evidence. Unlike v1's corresponding discussion, Section 5.2 attributes leadership results to models absent from Table 2, while Table 2 loses explanations of its retained ablation columns. The changed evaluator is also not explicitly reconciled with unchanged appendix validation results. These reporting regressions make the revised empirical claims harder to audit, outweighing the documentation gains.

A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same MICo-150K, MICo-Bench, and Qwen-MICo research. Their main text, equations, three tables, twenty figures, and appendices support comparison. v2's internal reporting inconsistencies do not constitute missing material.

Supplementary Section 6 also explains how source-target alignment and index collisions distinguish this problem from repetition in text-to-video extrapolation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Matched existing scores are unchanged, including Table 1's 8.97 instruction-following score and 76.36% success ratio for VideoCoF. v2 adds TokenFlow results, TGVE+ results including 20.90 PickScore and 0.956 CLIP-F, and V2VBench results including 5.024 frame quality. The underlying Chain-of-Frames construction, RoPE design, training objective and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that the retained benchmark scores use this acceleration.

P1.justification: v2 adds VideoCoF to the title, updates authorship and correspondence information, and corrects grammar and terminology. The supplement gains three sections and renames Discussion to Future Directions, while most existing prose and its narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two benchmark tables and two qualitative figures, inserts TokenFlow into Table 1, and reflows the supplement. T1.justification: The latent definitions, Equations 1–2, RoPE index construction and training mathematics are retained. The added RoPE discussion provides qualitative explanations and comparisons rather than new formal definitions, derivations or proofs.

improvement.justification: The added external benchmarks strengthen empirical support, and the documented extrapolation failure makes the account more credible than v1's infinite-extrapolation assertion. C2.justification: v2 explains how intrinsic dynamics mediate the effect of stochastic sampling and explicitly qualifies that sample-level DSD does not strongly correlate with correctness. The new sensitivity discussion identifies failure conditions at insufficient Koopman dimension and unrestricted DSD, refining the method's applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository address and identifies vLLM generation and Transformers log-probability/hidden-state computation in Algorithm 1. Table 3 revises the threshold and removes the previously disclosed minibatch size of 32. E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 2, and 5 and the multimodal method comparisons. The new DeepSeek-Math visualization is a diagnostic example, not an added competing method; the new citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes the reported DSD threshold from 25 to 10; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. E4.justification: v2 extends the existing analyses with t-SNE examples of correct and incorrect latent trajectories (Figure 7) and sensitivity tests for Koopman dimension and DSD threshold (Figure 11). Existing exploration-coefficient and component ablations, runtime analyses, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Mean@1 and mean@32 reporting remains unchanged. Neither version documents repeated training runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the added diagnostic plots introduce no stated uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6 retain their numerical results. The DSD traces in v1 Figure 7b are revised in v2 Figure 6b. New results show poor behavior at m=5 and reported collapse around 50 steps without thresholding, alongside new trajectory examples. These are diagnostic additions and revisions, not improved benchmark scores.

M1.justification: The learned and frozen Koopman dictionary, DSD definition, positive-advantage weighting, adaptive KL mechanism, and optimization objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 adds backend annotations and explicit log-probability computation, documenting implementation without establishing a new procedure.

Contributions are consolidated, the text-only training-dynamics discussion moves to the supplement, and the supplementary overview and qualitative-case ordering are reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adds two diagnostic figures, revises the DSD panel and its axis range, and relocates the former Figure 4 to supplementary Figure 8. It also rearranges case tables, boxes the supplementary overview, and removes a Table 3 row. Most existing graphics and table designs are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Generative Multimodal Models Are In-Context Learners, Show-o2, and Qwen3-Omni around the multimodal motivation. The related-work survey and positioning against token-level exploration methods remain substantively unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an explicit stochastic latent-state formulation, x_t = F(x_{t-1}, omega_t), with omega_t sampled from P_omega (v2 Equation 6). The Koopman approximation, DSD definition, residual formulation, and loss equations are otherwise retained; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity experiments address v1's untested choices of Koopman dimension and DSD threshold, while Figure 7 qualifies DSD's relationship to correctness. These modestly strengthen experimental support and interpretation. The gain is limited by removed minibatch information, the unexplained default-threshold revision, and unreconciled DSD traces between v2 Figures 6b and 10; benchmark evidence remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: information vanishes with depth, horizon position depends on task and model, and random pruning complements existing methods. The retitling and added supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: The new appendices attribute marginal scoring weaknesses to visual redundancy, sequence scoring weaknesses to error propagation, and harmful tokens to attention distraction. They also interpret the additional results as evidence of metric and architectural generality. These extend the earlier explanations, although Figure 13 contradicts the new claim that standalone scoring consistently matches or exceeds marginal scoring.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code availability from a future promise to a statement that code is available at the same repository. This is a reported access-status change; the PDFs retain the existing implementation, hardware, and pruning-setting disclosures.

E1.justification: The additions reuse existing tasks and datasets. InternVL3.5-8B is tested on the same six benchmarks used in Section 4.2; adding this model changes experimental configuration, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figures 13–14 add evaluated marginal-contribution and sequence-level alternatives against the original information metric. Comparator membership in the existing pruning benchmarks and Tables 1–3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments compare scoring variants with 72, 144, 288, and 432 retained tokens, using layer 3 on MME and layers 3 and 10 on TextVQA. Appendix 14 adds layer-wise evaluation of InternVL3.5-8B. Existing protocols and pruning settings in Tables 4–5 are retained; corrected MME axis labels do not establish a metric change.

E4.justification: New Appendices 12–14 substantially expand validation: they test sensitivity to singleton versus marginal contribution and first-token versus sequence-level scoring, examine attention distraction through a giraffe heatmap example, and test architectural generalization on InternVL3.5-8B. These address previously untested aspects of metric validity and mechanism.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing token-information distribution analysis is retained, and the additions introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and efficiency results remain unchanged, but Figures 13–16 add substantial diagnostic results. Figure 13 reports standalone versus marginal MME scores of 2304 versus 2176 at 72 tokens, but 2207 versus 2258 at 432 tokens. Further additions show first-token scoring outperforming sequence-level scoring, persistence of the sequence-level horizon, an attention-information mismatch, and task-dependent horizon curves for InternVL3.5-8B.

M1.justification: Appendix 12 introduces diagnostic scoring variants: marginal contribution removes a token from the full visual set, while sequence-level scoring averages ground-truth token probabilities across the answer. These change scoring procedures in the added tests; the original first-token score, Equations 1–6, and hybrid random-pruning procedures remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, author order, contact presentation, acknowledgments, and an appendix cross-reference are edited, and three focused appendix sections are appended. The existing scientific narrative and section sequence remain largely verbatim rather than extensively rewritten or reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 13–16 for metric comparisons, sequence-level behavior, heatmaps, and InternVL results. Several existing MME plots replace 'Accuracy' with 'Total Score', and baseline legends are adjusted. Page spacing and flow change modestly, while existing figure designs and table structures are largely preserved.

R1.justification: v2 adds the InternVL3.5 reference to support the new architecture experiment. Existing related-work discussions and positioning against VTW, PDrop, and other pruning methods remain substantively unchanged; subsequent citation renumbering is cosmetic.

T1.justification: Appendix 12 adds mathematical definitions in prose for marginal-contribution and sequence-level information, changing the reference token set and probability aggregation respectively. The original formal definitions and Equations 1–6 are unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, Appendices 12–14 provide useful direct checks of the information metric and additional architectural validation, strengthening empirical support without altering the main results. Corrected MME labels and reported code availability also help. The gains are limited by overinterpretation: Figure 13 shows standalone scoring losing at 432 tokens despite the claimed consistent superiority, and the heatmap illustrates attention distraction without establishing the asserted causal correction mechanism.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same visual-token information and pruning study despite the changed title. All 13 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds alternative-metric experiments, an attention-versus-information case study, and InternVL3.5-8B results.

It also connects register-token benefits to reduced feature norms. v1's detailed temporal-modeling and geometry-supervision future-work discussion is condensed.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the 0.01 pruning threshold, specifies RTX 4090 hardware and single-image timing for the rendering analysis, and states that the register ablation reuses the main ablation configuration. E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The standard deviations introduced in Table 17 specify injected pose noise, not uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for ScanNet++, pruning, register tokens, theoretical FLOPs and noisy poses. Other figures largely retain their content, with renumbering, table relocation and local layout adjustments.

R1.justification: v2 adds ScanNet++ and Depth Anything 3 references and positions MVP as a foundation for future pose-free extensions. It removes the dynamic-view-synthesis and 4D Gaussian Splatting citations associated with the shortened conclusion. The principal related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The pruning, register-token and pose-noise studies provide useful evidence about efficiency, design choices and applicability, while ScanNet++ adds external-dataset validation. T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and loss formulations, including Equation (7) and supplementary Section C, are unchanged. Correcting translator labels in Figure 2 does not alter the underlying mathematics.

improvement.justification: Figure 2 now matches Equation (7)'s translator directions and explicitly depicts the previously described cross-type attention connections. These corrections modestly improve technical clarity and internal consistency; the method, experimental evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIMOS and contain 17 readable pages, including supplementary Sections A–F and references. Text, equations, tables, and figures support a complete comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, qualitative comparisons, and main-text and supplementary ablations reported in v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original DIMOS benchmark results in Table 2, component and backbone ablations in Tables 3–4, and supplementary analyses in Figure 5 and Tables 7–9.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.
